A personal money judgment resting only on newspaper publication against a defendant who has left the state intending not to return is void, in the rendering state as well as elsewhere; substituted service must be the form most likely to reach the defendant.

A municipal ordinance that bars a person from occupying property solely because of race is not a legitimate exercise of the police power and violates the Fourteenth Amendment's protection of the rights to acquire, use and dispose of property.

Absent contrary legislation, a federal court has inherent power to appoint an auditor without the parties' consent to clarify complicated accounts and make tentative findings, and doing so is consistent with the Seventh Amendment if the jury keeps the final determination of the facts.

A defendant must interpose its defenses in the first suit, but under a permissive cross-complaint rule it need not assert an affirmative claim against the plaintiff there, and the earlier judgment does not bar a later action on that claim.

Under code pleading, an allegation that a draft was accepted for valuable consideration states an ultimate, issuable fact rather than a legal conclusion, and the particular consideration need not be pleaded.

A claim created by state law can arise under federal law when a substantial federal question, resting on a reasonable foundation and more than merely colorable, appears in the plaintiff's own statement of the claim and is necessary to the relief sought.

Under the South Carolina code, joined causes of action must each affect all parties to the action, so spouses with separate personal claims arising from one incident cannot sue jointly, because neither has a legal interest in the other's recovery.

When a later suit between the same parties involves a different demand, a fact, question, or right distinctly put in issue and directly determined in the earlier suit is conclusive, even if the earlier determination rested on an erroneous view of the law.

A counterclaim arises out of the transaction that is the subject matter of the suit when it is logically related to the opposing claim, even though the facts are not identical; transaction is a flexible term.

A state may treat a nonresident's driving on its highways as appointing a state official to receive service in suits arising from that driving, provided the statute requires actual receipt of notice and affords reasonable time to defend.

A statute authorizing substituted service on a state official for a nonresident motorist must itself require communication reasonably likely to inform the defendant; actual notice not required by the statute does not cure the defect.

Under the approach then prevailing under Swift v. Tyson, a federal court sitting in diversity could exercise independent judgment on a question of general common law despite contrary state decisions, and an actual reincorporation in another state to create diversity was not improper or collusive.

A defendant that specially appears, fully litigates personal jurisdiction, loses, and lets the judgment become final cannot relitigate that jurisdictional question by collateral attack when the judgment is sued upon elsewhere, absent fraud.
A party who knowingly uses part of an entire, indivisible demand as a defense to defeat an opponent's suit cannot reserve the remainder of that demand for a later affirmative action.

A United States citizen residing abroad remains subject to American laws made applicable to him, including the duty to return and testify when properly summoned, and may be penalized for refusal after appropriate notice and an opportunity to be heard.

A federal trial judge may comment on the evidence and express an opinion on the facts if the jury is told the facts are theirs to decide, but may not distort or add to the evidence; a disclaimer does not cure such an addition.

Under Hurn’s pre-Gibbs test, a court with a substantial federal claim could decide a non-federal ground for the same cause of action, even after the federal ground failed, but not a separate non-federal cause of action.
A state-law cause of action that incorporates a federal safety standard as an element of liability does not thereby arise under federal law for purposes of original federal jurisdiction.

A party that obtained all the relief it sought may not appeal from the decree in its favor merely to obtain review of findings it dislikes, and such findings do not operate as res judicata in the specified later proceedings.

The Seventh Amendment permits judgment for a defendant after a plaintiff's jury verdict when the trial judge expressly reserved the defendant's sufficiency motions and took the verdict subject to their resolution.

A court may order a judgment debtor to pay installments from income after allowing for reasonable needs and may punish refusal to comply as contempt; that enforces obedience to a court order the debtor can obey and is not imprisonment for debt.

When an unconditional acceleration clause has made every installment of a note due, the debt is a single indivisible claim, and a creditor who takes judgment for only part of it cannot later sue for or rely on the remainder.

A judgment obtained by serving a defendant who was fraudulently induced to enter the state for service is void for want of personal jurisdiction and may be attacked collaterally when its enforcement is sought in another state.

Where no federal constitutional or statutory law supplies the substantive rule, a federal court sitting in diversity must apply state law, including authoritative state judicial decisions as well as statutes; there is no general federal common law.

A prevailing party ordinarily may not appeal a favorable judgment to challenge unnecessary findings, but may appeal to have an unnecessary adverse adjudication removed from the operative decree itself.

Statutory interpleader requires only diversity between adverse claimants, so a disinterested stakeholder who deposits the property and shares citizenship with one claimant does not defeat jurisdiction; and interpleader does not reopen jurisdictional issues already litigated and decided between the claimants.

A statute authorizing a reviewing court to set aside a verdict as against the manifest weight of the evidence and require a new jury trial does not violate the state constitutional right to jury trial, provided the power is exercised within strict limits.

A state may render a personal judgment against its domiciliary who is absent from the state if he is served by a statutory method reasonably calculated to give actual notice and an opportunity to be heard, and another state cannot refuse that judgment recognition by reexamining its merits.

Parties who had notice and an opportunity to contest a court's jurisdiction, including the constitutionality of the statute conferring it, cannot collaterally attack the final decree; res judicata reaches jurisdictional objections that could have been raised.

Under its bankruptcy power, Congress may by a specific statute withdraw another court's power to proceed against a protected debtor, so that its later actions are void and open to collateral attack even if the debtor never contested jurisdiction or appealed there.

An absent party is indispensable only if any decree the court could render would inevitably affect that party's interest; a necessary party whose interest is separable should ordinarily be joined, but the court keeps jurisdiction to proceed without that party.

Due process forbids binding a person to a judgment in an earlier representative action unless the parties to that action adequately represented that person's interests; a state's labelling a suit a class action does not settle its power to bind absentees.

A court may mould an informal verdict so that its form implements the substance the jury agreed upon only when the jury's real purpose and intent appear clearly, sufficiently, and convincingly; an uncertain or ambiguous verdict cannot be moulded and requires a new trial.

A motion for judgment notwithstanding the verdict tests legal sufficiency with the evidence viewed for the verdict winner, but on a new-trial motion the trial judge may set aside a verdict against the clear weight of the evidence, resting on false evidence, or producing a miscarriage of justice.

Under a removal statute authorizing removal by the defendant or defendants, an original state-court plaintiff cannot remove on diversity grounds merely because the defendant asserts an independent counterclaim, and federal courts must keep removal jurisdiction within the limits Congress prescribed.

A federal rule is within the rulemaking authority Congress delegated if it genuinely regulates procedure, meaning the judicial process for enforcing substantive rights and administering remedies; the importance of the interest affected does not make a procedural rule substantive.

Mutuality is not required for issue preclusion: a judgment may be invoked by a stranger to it, so long as the issue is identical, the judgment was final on the merits, and the party against whom it is asserted was a party or privy.
Liberal permission to join claims in one complaint does not require trying them together; a court should sever when a combined trial would confuse the jury or prejudice a party's substantial right.

Rule 14 allows a defendant to implead a party who is or may be liable to it for the plaintiff's claim before the defendant has suffered any loss; the contingent claim is determined in the same action and enforcement is stayed until state law's conditions are met.

Directing a verdict when the claimant's proof leaves an essential fact to speculation rather than reasonable inference does not violate the Seventh Amendment, which preserves the fundamental jury institution rather than every procedural detail.

Federal law governs the United States' rights and duties on commercial paper it issues in exercising its constitutional and statutory functions, and absent an applicable Act of Congress federal courts may fashion the governing rule.

Despite the ordinary finality of judgments, equity permits relief from a judgment obtained through a deliberately planned scheme of fraud on the court, and an appellate court so defrauded may vacate its own judgment where the fraud is undisputed.

A fact determined in an earlier suit, whether ultimate or mediate there, cannot be used in a later suit to establish conclusively a mediate datum from which a different ultimate fact is to be inferred.

Under the Federal Rules a complaint need only give a short and plain statement showing entitlement to relief under Rule 8(a); the old formulation requiring facts sufficient to constitute a cause of action is not the governing pleading formula.

Under California's broadened interpleader statute, a disinterested tenant facing competing claims to the same lease royalties may interplead its landlord and an adverse claimant, despite the rule barring a tenant from denying the landlord's title, if it alleges facts showing a reasonable probability of competing demands.

A federal court in diversity may not disregard a state limitations rule that would bar recovery on the same state-created claim in state court; the test is whether ignoring the state rule would substantially change the outcome so far as legal rules determine it.

An absent defendant may be subjected to a personal judgment when it has minimum contacts with the forum such that maintaining the suit does not offend traditional notions of fair play and substantial justice.

A reviewing court may not reweigh conflicting evidence or substitute its own inference for the jury's; only when there is a complete absence of probative facts to support the jury's conclusion does reversible error appear.

Federal jury officials may not systematically and intentionally exclude an eligible group, such as daily wage earners, from the jury lists; hardship may justify excusing an individual juror but not excluding a whole class.

A pleading must state facts rather than legal conclusions or evidence: a defendant's belief that a publication was true does not plead truth, and absolute privilege must be shown by pleaded facts, though it need not be named.

Under the Second Circuit's approach in 1946, summary judgment is improper where there is the slightest doubt as to the facts, particularly where the outcome turns on the credibility of a witness whom the jury has not seen testify.

Witness statements, memoranda and mental impressions that a lawyer prepares in anticipation of litigation, though outside attorney-client privilege, cannot be obtained in discovery as of right; the party seeking them must show adequate reasons, such as necessity, for the intrusion.

When an amendment replaces an exclusively equitable claim with one seeking only money, the jury right first arises with the amendment, and a jury demand made within the prescribed period after that amendment is timely.

Because each tax year is a separate claim, a prior tax judgment operates in a later year only as collateral estoppel, which requires an identical matter and unchanged controlling facts and legal rules.

A state court hearing a federal claim may not use strict local pleading rules to defeat the federal right; the Court will independently construe the complaint to decide whether it states a claim under federal law.

A defendant who has answered on the merits does not default under Rule 55 merely by failing to attend trial after counsel withdraws; the plaintiff must still prove the case, and a judgment entered without due process may be resisted when its enforcement is sought.

A motion for judgment notwithstanding the verdict raises a question of law about whether evidence, if believed, authorizes the verdict, while a new-trial motion invokes the trial judge's discretion to set aside a verdict he considers against the weight of the evidence.

When all the facts necessary to a legal consequence have been pleaded and contested, a court may apply that consequence, including a statute, even though the party did not expressly plead the legal conclusion; stating it is proper and desirable but not mandatory.

A state statute requiring a small shareholder to post security for the corporation's expenses in a derivative suit is substantive and binds a federal diversity court; Cohen is also the origin of the collateral-order doctrine, under which the order refusing security was immediately appealable.

In a diversity action on a state-created claim, a state rule making service an integral part of the limitations scheme governs the life of the claim; filing under Federal Rule 3 does not give the claim a longer life than state law allows.

A litigant whom state law bars from maintaining an action in the state's courts cannot obtain a more favorable enforcement opportunity on a state-law claim by invoking diversity jurisdiction in a federal court in that state.

Under the Missouri provision requiring items of special damage to be specifically stated, an injury neither pleaded nor a necessary result of a pleaded injury cannot be proved over objection, even where the defendant had actual advance knowledge of it.

The Declaratory Judgment Act enlarges the remedies available in federal court but does not extend jurisdiction; a declaratory suit arises under federal law only if the underlying claim would, not because the plaintiff anticipates a federal defense.

Before a proceeding that is to be accorded finality, due process requires notice reasonably calculated, under all the circumstances, to apprise interested parties of the pendency of the action and afford them an opportunity to present their objections.

Under the Full Faith and Credit Clause, a state that hears wrongful-death actions for local deaths may not categorically close its otherwise competent courts to a sister state's wrongful-death claim, at least where the litigation has close connections to the forum.
A federal judge sitting in diversity must anticipate how the state's highest court would rule, rather than develop independently what seems equitable or sound public policy.

A complaint that shows an intended claim the defendant can reasonably understand survives a motion to dismiss even if imperfectly stated, and a conditional privilege must be raised as an affirmative defense, while an absolute privilege disclosed by the complaint bars the claim.

A nonresident who entered a county voluntarily, not in response to criminal process, and is then arrested and jailed there is not immune from service of civil process while confined awaiting trial on the criminal charge.

Federal law governs the validity of a release of Federal Employers' Liability Act rights even in state court, and a state that provides jury trials for such negligence actions may not take the disputed question of fraudulent procurement from the jury.

Summary judgment is proper against a party who bears the trial burden, has no admissible affirmative proof, and relies only on the possibility that the demeanor of witnesses who all deny the essential fact would persuade a jury of the opposite.

When a foreign corporation carries on continuous and systematic corporate activities in a state, due process permits, but does not require, that state to exercise jurisdiction over it on causes of action entirely distinct from those activities.

The Arkansas Supreme Court rejected the local-action rule for this interstate controversy, holding that an Arkansas court may hear a damages claim for injury to real property in another state; its central concern was that the defendant could otherwise escape any remedy.

Where a free-pass holder has released the carrier from liability, the carrier's duty is only to refrain from willful or wanton injury, and summary judgment is proper when the plaintiff cannot show knowledge of the particular defect that caused the accident.

A person whose rights would inevitably be affected by the judgment is an indispensable party who must be joined, even in an action framed only as one for damages against someone else, and refusal to join her warrants dismissal.

As decided in 1953, an agreement made before any controversy arose to arbitrate claims under section 12(2) of the Securities Act of 1933 was void under the Act's nonwaiver provision, section 14, because the investor's right to select a judicial forum could not be waived.

Under the Kansas real-party-in-interest statute, once an insurer has fully paid a loss the subrogated claim belongs wholly to the insurer, which must bring the action in its own name; the insured cannot sue for the insurer's benefit.

A matter actually litigated and essential to a final judgment binds the parties in a different cause of action, and a finding necessary to the decree may be appealed even by the party who prevailed on the original claim.

Alienage jurisdiction requires the plaintiff to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the opposing party is a citizen or subject of a particular foreign state; a stateless person is not within the statutory grant merely because he is not American.

Notice by mailing, posting and publication that complies with a statute does not satisfy due process when the authorities know the owner is mentally incompetent, cannot understand the proceeding, and has no guardian to act for her.

Federal common law under Clearfield Trust does not govern a dispute between private parties over government paper when the United States' rights and duties are not at stake and any effect on federal interests is speculative and remote; state law governs.

In a multiple-claims action, a final decision on an individual claim is appealable under section 1291 when the district court expressly determines there is no just reason for delay and expressly directs entry of judgment under Rule 54(b).

Under amended Rule 54(b), a finally adjudicated claim may be certified and appealed even though an unresolved counterclaim arises partly from the same transactions; the relationship is a factor for the district court's discretion, not a jurisdictional bar.

A property owner is entitled to a hearing on just compensation, and newspaper publication alone is constitutionally inadequate notice of that hearing when the owner's name is known to the condemning authority and appears in official records.

A party cannot secure personal service on an otherwise out-of-reach nonresident by fraud, trickery, artifice or a wrongful device, used by the party or someone acting for the party, that induces the person to enter the court's territorial jurisdiction; such service will be set aside.

A federal court applying state law must predict how the state's highest court would decide today, and may decline to follow an old state holding that has not been overruled when recent considered dicta of that court indicate it would no longer be followed.

Under the New Jersey constitution a court may use additur, conditioning denial of a plaintiff's new-trial motion on the defendant's consent to an increased award, but its use is reviewable for abuse of discretion or manifest denial of justice.

A court of appeals that may eventually hear an appeal may issue mandamus under the All Writs Act in exceptional circumstances, and calendar congestion, complexity and trial length are not exceptional conditions permitting reference of a whole nonjury case to a master.

A tort claim merges into a final sister-state judgment, which is a debt and a distinct cause of action, so the forum must enforce the judgment under full faith and credit even though its own law has abolished the underlying tort.

Under Rule 8(a)(2) a complaint needs only a short and plain statement giving fair notice of the claim and its grounds, and should not be dismissed unless it appears beyond doubt that no set of supporting facts could entitle the claimant to relief.

Due process permits a state to exercise personal jurisdiction over a foreign insurer in a suit on a contract that has a substantial connection with the state, even when that single contract is the insurer's only shown business there.

A single wrongful act that causes both personal injury and property damage to the same person gives rise to one cause of action with different items of damages, so a judgment on part of it bars a later action for the rest.

Rule 13(g), as the Third Circuit read it in 1958, allows a crossclaim only as ancillary to a claim already asserted against the crossclaimant, so coplaintiffs cannot crossclaim against each other on an independent claim from the same accident.

In diversity, a state rule on the mode of enforcing a state right that is not shown to be integral to that right yields to a strong countervailing federal interest, such as the federal judge-jury allocation, even though the outcome might differ.

A State may exercise personal jurisdiction over a nonresident defendant only if the defendant purposefully availed itself of conducting activities in the State, invoking the benefits and protections of its law; the unilateral activity of another person cannot supply the connection.

An erroneous jury instruction does not support reversal unless counsel distinctly objected to the actual charge before the jury retired, stating the matter and the grounds, so that the trial judge had a meaningful chance to correct it.

When legal and equitable claims in one action share common factual issues, the court's discretion over the order of trial must be used to preserve the jury right on the legal claim, which can be lost through a prior equitable determination only in the most imperative circumstances.

A passenger on an ordinary commercial aircraft flying through the regular navigable airspace above a state is within that state's territorial limits and may be personally served there under then-Rule 4(f).

A federal diversity court may retain jurisdiction but stay an eminent-domain action pending a prompt authoritative state-court construction of an uncertain state statute governing a city's condemnation power; difficulty of state law alone does not justify surrendering jurisdiction.
A judgment is not void under Rule 60(b)(4) merely because it was erroneous on a jurisdictional point the court adjudicated, and Rule 60(b) is no substitute for an appeal the party failed to pursue.

A juror commits misconduct by giving fellow jurors private, specialized knowledge as original evidence of material facts not introduced at trial, and reversal is required where the misconduct is material and probably caused injury.

In a diversity case, a federal court should decline discretionary relief under the federal Declaratory Judgments Act when granting it would conflict with a specific state substantive policy and no countervailing federal interest outweighs that policy.

A general denial is read in light of counsel's good-faith certification, so it will not be construed to deny a fact the defendant plainly knows to be true, such as its own state of incorporation, and that allegation stands admitted.

Under the version of § 1404(a) then in force, a transferee district had to be one where the plaintiff had a right to bring the action when suit began, independently of the defendant's later consent or waiver of venue and personal-jurisdiction objections.

An insurer facing tort claims that may exceed its policy limit may interplead the claimants under Rule 22 or the interpleader statute, even though it denies liability and the claims are unliquidated, because possible multiple liability on one inadequate fund is enough.

A complaint is read as a whole with its attached contract; where the only wrong and damages pleaded rest on a termination the contract expressly permits, liberal pleading rules do not supply an independent claim the complaint does not allege.

A trial judge's discretionary power under Rule 49(b) to submit written questions with a general verdict implies a power to withdraw them in proper cases, such as when a question is ambiguous and confusing, subject to review for abuse of discretion.

A plaintiff must prove by a preponderance both negligence and its proximate contribution to the injury; a jury verdict cannot stand where the evidence leaves causation to speculation among possible explanations.

A claim consists of the facts of an occurrence or transaction, not the legal theory chosen, so a judgment on that transaction bars a later suit on new theories, including one against principals whose liability derives from the agents sued first.

Under Rule 41(b), a dismissal for failure to satisfy a precondition to the court's reaching the merits is a dismissal for "lack of jurisdiction" and does not bar a new action, even when the order does not say "without prejudice".

An otherwise nonappealable order, such as the denial of a temporary restraining order, may be reviewed immediately as a final decision under § 1291 when it determines substantial rights that would be irreparably lost if review were delayed.

A tortious act under a long-arm statute includes the injury that completes the tort, and due process permits jurisdiction over a nonresident component maker whose product, placed in ordinary commercial distribution with use in the forum contemplated, causes injury there.

A signed and filed pretrial report that defines the issues and lists the witnesses binds the parties at trial as a Rule 16 pretrial order whatever its title, and the trial judge has discretion to refuse amendments and a continuance sought at trial.

Where federal law forces related claims to be litigated in two different districts, Rule 13(a) does not require a counterclaim common to both to be asserted in whichever action received the first responsive pleading; once adjudicated in one, it cannot be reasserted in the other.

A federal trial court has inherent power to dismiss an action with prejudice for failure to prosecute on its own initiative, without a defendant's motion under Rule 41(b), and a client is bound by the acts and omissions of freely chosen counsel.

Where legal and equitable claims are joined, a timely jury demand on legal issues cannot be denied because those issues are called incidental to equitable ones, and legal issues must be tried to a jury before final disposition of equitable claims sharing them.

A decree that disposes of the whole complaint and unconditionally orders full divestiture is a final judgment for purposes of appeal even though the detailed plan for carrying out the divestiture remains to be formulated.

A federal court applying state law must decide as the state's highest court would, and may follow that court's recent considered dicta over an older contrary holding when the dicta signal the old rule no longer stands.

When an affected property owner's name and address are known or easily ascertainable, newspaper publication and posted notices are constitutionally inadequate; notice must be reasonably calculated, in the actual circumstances, to inform the owner of the proceeding.

Under the 1962 version of Rule 24(a)(2), a shareholder has no right to intervene in a corporation's suit unless he may be legally bound by the judgment and representation may be inadequate; disagreement over how to conduct the litigation is not inadequate representation.

Summary judgment should be used cautiously in complex antitrust litigation where motive and intent are central, the proof lies largely with the alleged conspirators and credibility may matter; the record must be viewed favorably to the party opposing the motion.

Under the historical Rule 49(b), when answers to interrogatories are consistent with each other but conflict with the general verdict, the court may enter judgment on the answers, return the jury for further consideration, or order a new trial, after first attempting a fair reconciliation.

An execution officer must protect both creditor and debtor: real estate susceptible of division must be divided and only enough sold to satisfy the execution, and a sale of the whole in violation of that requirement may be cancelled in equity on condition of restitution.

A finding in an earlier action does not bind a party in later litigation unless it was a material basis for the earlier judgment; a finding adverse to a party who won the judgment, and so could not appeal it, is not conclusive.

A judgment is entitled to full faith and credit even on questions of subject-matter jurisdiction when the second court's inquiry shows those questions were fully and fairly litigated and finally decided in the court that rendered it.

A deliberate and willful refusal to obey discovery orders warrants default and dismissal of counterclaims with prejudice, and a party that appeared and litigated before willfully defaulting may face an amended, increased demand for unliquidated damages, to be assessed at a hearing.

Under code pleading, a complaint must state the material, essential, ultimate facts that constitute the cause of action, not merely the pleader's legal conclusions such as assault, trespass, or malicious confinement.

A suit arises under the Copyright Act for 28 U.S.C. § 1338 only if it seeks a remedy the Act expressly grants, requires construction of the Act, or, more doubtfully, involves a distinctive copyright policy requiring federal principles to control.

Rule 35 permits a mental or physical examination of any party, defendant as well as plaintiff, but only on an affirmative showing that each condition is genuinely in controversy and that there is good cause for each particular examination.

A judgment entered on proof after a defendant who has answered fails to appear at trial is a judgment on the merits, not a default judgment, so the notice of application for default required by Rule 55(b) does not apply.

A district court's certification under 28 U.S.C. § 1292(b) does not ensure an immediate appeal; the court of appeals may deny leave where early review would prolong rather than advance the litigation and the error can be corrected after final judgment.

Summary judgment is improper where the disputed material facts turn on motive, intent and the credibility of the moving party's own witnesses; the opponent is entitled to test that account by cross-examination before the trier of fact.

Contracting parties may agree in advance to submit to a court's jurisdiction, and a person a contract designates to receive process is an agent authorized by appointment under the Federal Rule when she promptly accepts and transmits the process, even without an express promise to do so.

A prospective juror biased or prejudiced for or against a party, including bias about the subject matter of the litigation, is disqualified as a matter of law, and the juror's assurance of fairness in response to leading questions does not cure it.

Because liability and damages are ordinarily intertwined, a new trial granted for an error affecting liability should extend to all issues where damages are unliquidated; a limited new trial is disfavored.

A federal judge may comment on the evidence, but may not tell a deadlocked jury his own view of the ultimate disputed fact, because that amounts to an instructed verdict even when he says the comment is not binding.
A trial court may grant a new trial only on the grounds enumerated in the procedural rules and has no power to order one on a free-standing ground of the interests of justice.

When a Federal Rule actually covers the disputed issue, a federal diversity court applies it unless it exceeds the Rules Enabling Act or the Constitution; ordinary Erie analysis, guided by forum shopping and inequitable administration, applies only when no Federal Rule covers the issue.

Where the basic facts and the accepted professional practice are undisputed, a trial judge's conclusion on negligence is, on Hicks's 1966 reasoning, a legal conclusion freely reviewable on appeal rather than a finding subject to the clearly-erroneous standard.

A trial court does not abuse its discretion in granting a new trial where a single undifferentiated verdict on two distinct causes of action leaves liability and damages on each unascertainable, even though no party objected to the verdict form before the verdict.
To justify a new trial, newly discovered evidence must concern facts existing at the time of trial, so a medical treatment developed after trial does not qualify.

Where a judgment was obtained in part through perjured testimony, the court may not preserve it by weighing how much the perjury mattered; denying Rule 60(b) relief when the record clearly supports the showing of perjury is an abuse of discretion.

A federal court has pendent power over a state claim when the federal claim is substantial, both claims arise from a common nucleus of operative fact, and a plaintiff would ordinarily be expected to try them together; exercising that power remains discretionary.

The verification requirement for shareholder derivative actions does not justify dismissing a bona fide complaint because the shareholder does not personally understand it, when she verified it in good faith reliance on careful investigation by trusted advisers and counsel.

Neither the Seventh Amendment nor Rule 50 bars a court of appeals from directing judgment for the verdict loser after finding the evidence insufficient, though it must consider proper grounds for a new trial.

Mandamus is reserved for exceptional circumstances amounting to judicial usurpation of power; an asserted error in an interlocutory discovery order, even one the government may have no ordinary opportunity to appeal, does not by itself justify the writ.

A class action under California section 382 requires an ascertainable class and a well-defined community of interest in questions of law and fact; it does not require a common fund or a single indivisible recovery.

Statutory interpleader under section 1335 requires only minimal diversity among adverse claimants and is available before tort claims are reduced to judgment, but the injunction it supports must be limited to protecting the interpleaded fund.

Under Rule 19(b), whether an action may proceed without a person who cannot be joined is a contextual judgment of equity and good conscience weighing the interests of plaintiff, defendant, absentee and public; indispensability is the conclusion of that analysis, not a label preceding it.

Under New York's Schwartz formulation, a party is precluded from relitigating an identical issue that was necessarily decided earlier and is decisive now if that party had a full and fair opportunity to contest it, even when the present claimants were absent from the earlier action.

Under 28 U.S.C. § 1359, a district court lacks jurisdiction when a claim is assigned to a nominal assignee who pays token consideration and returns nearly all the recovery to the assignor in order to create diversity.

Separate and distinct claims of class members may not be aggregated to satisfy the jurisdictional amount under § 1332; aggregation is allowed only where plaintiffs enforce a single title or right in which they have a common and undivided interest.

Under Rule 13(g) and (h), crossclaims and claims against added parties arise from the same transaction or occurrence as the original action when they are logically related to it, and Rule 42(b) separate trials can manage any resulting complexity.

On a three-judge plurality's analysis, a person whose practical interest may be impaired and inadequately represented by existing parties can intervene under Rule 24(a)(2), even to appeal after judgment, but only to challenge decree provisions that actually affect that interest.

Absent an extraordinary situation requiring special protection of a governmental or creditor interest, prejudgment garnishment of wages without notice and a prior opportunity to be heard violates procedural due process, even though the deprivation is temporary.

The United States may sue without express statutory authorization to enjoin a widespread practice of obtaining default judgments without proper service, where the practice substantially burdens interstate commerce or deprives many people of property without due process through state action.
The Seventh Amendment jury right extends to those issues in a shareholder derivative suit on which the corporation would have been entitled to a jury had it sued directly.

A party moving for summary judgment bears the initial burden of showing the absence of a genuine issue of material fact, and if its own showing leaves a gap the motion must be denied even though the opponent offers no competent evidence in response.

A counterclaim is compulsory under Rule 13(a) when it bears a logical relationship to the opposing party's claim, and a compulsory counterclaim falls within ancillary federal jurisdiction without an independent jurisdictional ground.

Compliance with a state's service procedures, including registering to do business and appointing a service agent, does not itself establish constitutional jurisdiction over claims that arose elsewhere and are unconnected with the corporation's limited forum activities.

A defendant charged with infringing a patent previously declared invalid may plead that judgment as an estoppel against the patentee, even though the defendant was not a party to the first suit, unless the patentee shows it lacked a full and fair opportunity to litigate.

Due process ordinarily requires notice and a hearing before a creditor may attach a debtor's property before judgment; a statute allowing summary attachment without limits tied to extraordinary need, and reaching necessities of life, is unconstitutional.

Under Rule 24(a)(2) the burden of showing that existing representation may be inadequate is minimal; a union member may intervene in the Secretary of Labor's LMRDA election suit, limited to the grounds in the Secretary's complaint and to the remedy.

Federal courts sitting in admiralty treat a freely agreed forum-selection clause as prima facie valid and enforce it unless the resisting party shows that enforcement would be unreasonable or unjust or that the clause is invalid for fraud or overreaching.

Due process requires notice and an opportunity to be heard before a State helps a private claimant seize goods in another person's possession, even temporarily and even where title is disputed, except in extraordinary situations.

Under the rule Zahn announced, each plaintiff in a Rule 23(b)(3) diversity class action asserting a separate and distinct claim had to satisfy the jurisdictional amount; a qualifying plaintiff's claim could not supply jurisdiction over another's deficient claim.
A six-person jury in a federal civil case satisfies the Seventh Amendment, which preserves the substance of the common-law jury right rather than every historical incident such as a jury of twelve.

Mandamus may be used to review an order requiring the President to submit subpoenaed materials for in camera inspection, and presidential communications are presumptively but not absolutely privileged, so the presumption yields to a particular and compelling grand-jury need.

The Seventh Amendment applies to statutory causes of action that enforce legal rights and seek legal remedies in the ordinary courts, so either party may demand a jury in a federal Title VIII action for actual and punitive damages.

Under the Alaska Constitution's due process clause, a summons must give the information the defendant needs for a meaningful opportunity to respond; a small-claims summons to distant indigent defendants that omits the option of a written response is inadequate.

A creditor with a lien may obtain sequestration of the debtor's goods without prior notice or hearing where a judge issues the writ on a verified factual showing, the creditor posts bond, and the debtor may obtain an immediate hearing at which the creditor bears the burden.

An order refusing to quash a subpoena is ordinarily appealable only after contempt, but an order directing the President to produce evidence is immediately appealable under section 1291; a generalized claim of executive privilege yields to a demonstrated, specific need for criminal-trial evidence.

In a Rule 23(b)(3) class action, individual notice must be sent to all class members identifiable through reasonable effort, the representative plaintiff ordinarily bears its cost, and a court may not conduct a preliminary merits inquiry to shift that cost to defendants.

For diversity purposes a natural person is a citizen of a state only if a United States citizen domiciled there; domicile persists until the person takes up residence elsewhere intending to remain, and citizenship is determined when the complaint is filed.

Rule 20(a) permits joinder of plaintiffs when their rights to relief arise from the same transaction, occurrence, or series of logically related transactions or occurrences and a common question of law or fact will arise.

In this historical New York trial ruling, a nonresident individual who continuously and substantially conducted business in New York and derived substantial revenue there was held subject to jurisdiction under CPLR 301 on a claim unrelated to that business.

Prejudgment garnishment that freezes a debtor's property, including a corporation's bank account, violates due process when the writ issues from a clerk on a conclusory affidavit, without judicial participation or an early hearing at which the creditor must justify the restraint.

A determination of liability that leaves damages and other requested relief unresolved is interlocutory, and Rule 54(b) cannot make it a final decision, because a complaint asserting one legal right is a single claim even though it requests several remedies.

Under New York CPLR 301, a nonresident who continuously does business in New York is subject to jurisdiction there even on claims not arising locally, and a foreign parent is reached through service on a New York subsidiary that is its alter ego.

Dismissal under Rule 37(b)(2) for disobeying discovery orders is within the district court's discretion where the record supports findings of willfulness, bad faith or fault, and severe sanctions serve to deter other litigants as well as to punish the offender.

Mandamus is an extraordinary remedy reserved for exceptional circumstances, and it will not issue to overturn a discovery order when the petitioner has another adequate means of obtaining the relief it wants, such as asserting a specific privilege claim and seeking in camera review.

Pendent-party jurisdiction requires both that Article III permit it and that Congress has not expressly or implicitly negated it in the jurisdictional statute; a state claim against a county excluded from section 1983 could not be appended to section 1983 claims against its officials.

Subject-matter jurisdiction concerns a court's competence to entertain the category of action, not the plaintiff's ability to establish the substantive conditions for relief, so an error about a statutory element of the claim does not render the judgment void.

When Congress creates statutory public rights that the Government enforces in its sovereign capacity, it may assign initial adjudication and factfinding to an administrative forum with which a jury would be incompatible, without violating the Seventh Amendment.

Postjudgment body execution against a tort debtor is constitutional only with findings of probable cause that the debtor is fleeing or concealing assets, and with a prompt hearing on the debtor's petition for release.

Leave to amend under Rule 15(a) is to be freely given when justice requires, and the party opposing amendment bears the burden of showing prejudice, assessed in the particular circumstances rather than assumed whenever an admission is withdrawn.

Assertions of state-court jurisdiction over property, whether labeled in rem or quasi in rem, must be evaluated under International Shoe and its progeny; the mere statutory presence of property unrelated to the claim does not supply sufficient contacts.

A request for class members' names and addresses made solely to send notice is governed by Rule 23(d), not the discovery rules, and the representative plaintiff ordinarily bears the cost of identification even when the defendant is ordered to do the work.

An order refusing or withdrawing class certification is not a final decision appealable as of right under 28 U.S.C. section 1291, under either the collateral-order doctrine or the death-knell doctrine.

Where individual suits over a defendant's uniform rules could impose incompatible standards of conduct on it or impair absent members' interests, a class may be certified under Rule 23(b)(1) without opt-out rights, even if it would also qualify under Rule 23(b)(3).

In a diversity action, ancillary jurisdiction does not extend to the plaintiff's direct state-law claim against an impleaded third-party defendant who shares her citizenship, because § 1332 requires complete diversity and Rule 14 cannot supply subject-matter jurisdiction.

A parent who acquiesces in his child's move to live with the other parent in another state has not thereby purposefully sought that state's benefits and protections, so due process bars that state from exercising personal jurisdiction over him in a child-support action.

Under Rule 15(b), an unpleaded issue is tried by implied consent only if the record shows the opposing party recognized it was being litigated and had a fair chance to contest it; evidence relevant to an already pleaded issue does not establish consent.

Under Rule 37 a severe discovery sanction, such as precluding proof of damages, may be imposed for fault short of willfulness, including counsel's gross negligence in failing to obey discovery orders, though not for a genuine inability to comply.

Federal trial courts have broad discretion to permit offensive nonmutual issue preclusion unless the plaintiff could easily have joined the earlier action or its use would be unfair to the defendant, and applying it to an issue decided in an equitable action does not violate the Seventh Amendment.

As this 1979 district decision held before being reversed, federal common law may govern private tort claims, and so support § 1331 jurisdiction, upon weighing substantial federal interests, the effect of applying state law on them, and the effect of displacing state law.
Federal law governs the priority of liens arising from federal lending programs, but absent a need for a nationally uniform rule the federal rule of decision adopts nondiscriminatory state law.

Adjudicative administrative findings can have issue-preclusive effect, but preclusion yields where there is a clear and convincing need to redetermine an issue because of its effect on the public or on persons absent from the original proceeding.

A nonparty that controls litigation protecting its own direct financial or proprietary interest is bound by the issues actually adjudicated there, absent a different issue, a material change in controlling facts or law, or other special circumstances.

When investigation conducted without compulsory process gives a factual basis to believe a judgment offered as offensive collateral estoppel rested on a compromise verdict, jurors with relevant information may be deposed to resist its preclusive use.

A temporary restraining order may issue without notice under Rule 65(b) even when the adverse party could be notified, if specific facts show that giving notice would itself defeat the relief; the order must be narrow and brief.

Section 1983 does not displace conventional issue-preclusion principles or 28 U.S.C. § 1738; federal courts generally give a state judgment the preclusive effect the rendering state would, provided the party had a full and fair opportunity to litigate the issue.

A federal-common-law cause of action between private parties, which could support § 1331 jurisdiction, requires a specifically demonstrated significant conflict between state law and an identifiable federal policy; federal concern about the parties or events is not enough.

Jurisdiction requires a sufficient relationship among the particular defendant, the forum, and the litigation; garnishing an insurer's obligation to defend and indemnify cannot supply an insured's missing contacts, and contacts cannot be aggregated among defending parties.

Service on a corporation is valid when delivered to an employee so integrated with the organization that he will know what to do with the papers, even without express authorization; losing the papers internally afterward is not excusable neglect.

Service on a corporation is valid when the process server, acting reasonably, follows the directions of the corporation's own employees and delivers the papers to the person they identify as accepting process; a corporation may appoint such a recipient without formal designation.

An American citizen domiciled abroad is not a citizen of any State for diversity purposes, and a dual national who is a United States citizen ordinarily cannot invoke alienage jurisdiction through his foreign citizenship.

Federal Rule 15, not contrary state law, governs whether a plaintiff's later-acquired representative capacity may be pleaded and relate back to a timely federal complaint, and leave may not be denied for mere delay without prejudice.

Under Rule 54(b) a district court first determines that a claim is finally decided and then whether there is any just reason for delay; a pending nonfrivolous counterclaim does not bar certification, and the court's weighing of equities receives substantial deference.

A state may constitutionally exercise personal jurisdiction over a nonresident director of its corporation, under a director-consent statute, in an action for breach of fiduciary duty to that corporation, where the director accepted the office after the statute took effect.

In a diversity action on a state-law claim, Rule 3 does not govern tolling of the state statute of limitations; because no Federal Rule covers the issue, Erie requires applying the state rule that service, not filing, stops the limitations period.

Specific jurisdiction requires a defendant-created affiliation with the forum that gives reasonable advance notice of suit there; a consumer's post-sale travel with the product into the forum does not supply it, and the relevant foreseeability is anticipating suit from the defendant's own conduct.

Corporate attorney-client privilege is not limited to a control group: it protects confidential communications from employees to counsel, made at management's direction about matters within their duties, to obtain legal advice; work product revealing counsel's mental processes needs more than substantial need and undue hardship.

Under the plurality's formulation, a state may constitutionally apply its own law only if it has a significant contact or significant aggregation of contacts with the parties and the occurrence or transaction, creating state interests, so that choosing its law is neither arbitrary nor fundamentally unfair.

Due process does not require appointed counsel for an indigent parent in every termination proceeding; courts weigh the Mathews v. Eldridge factors case by case against a presumption that appointed counsel is owed only when physical liberty is at stake.

A federal court predicting unsettled state law should defer to a prediction already made by the court of appeals whose circuit includes that state, unless clear signals from the state's highest court convincingly show the prediction wrong.

A final judgment on the merits that was not appealed keeps its claim-preclusive effect even if it was erroneous or rested on a legal principle later rejected in another case; there is no simple-justice or public-policy exception to res judicata.

Rule 68's mandatory shifting of post-offer costs applies only when the plaintiff-offeree obtains a judgment less favorable than the offer; when the defendant wins outright, costs are governed by Rule 54(d).

A foreign forum's less favorable substantive law ordinarily receives neither conclusive nor substantial weight in the forum non conveniens inquiry, a foreign plaintiff's forum choice receives less deference, and a district court's reasonable balancing is reviewed only for clear abuse of discretion.

Rule 52(a)'s clearly erroneous standard governs a finding of discriminatory intent, with no exception for ultimate facts, and when a legal error has caused the trial court to omit findings the appellate court must ordinarily remand rather than find the facts itself.

Notice must be reasonably calculated under the circumstances to reach the person affected; posting an eviction notice on a tenant's door is inadequate where posted notices are known to be frequently removed and feasible measures such as mail could improve reliability.

A Title VII plaintiff seeking to represent a class must actually satisfy Rule 23(a), shown by rigorous analysis; membership in the same racial or national-origin group does not by itself make his claim common to or typical of other discrimination claims against the employer.

Under Rule 52(a) an appellate court must accept a trial court's findings of fact unless clearly erroneous, and may not substitute its own weighing of the evidence, though findings resting on a mistaken view of the governing law receive no such protection.

A forum state may apply its own collateral-estoppel rules to give a sister-state issue determination greater effect than the rendering state would, and judicial estoppel bars a party from contradicting a sworn position he successfully maintained in earlier litigation.

Title VII does not displace 28 U.S.C. section 1738, so a state-court judgment affirming a state agency's rejection of a discrimination claim receives in a later federal Title VII suit the preclusive effect it has in state court, provided the state proceedings satisfied due process.

A practitioner who undertakes a cure is culpable if the patient is impaired by his negligence or failure to attend within a reasonable time, but not merely because a cure diligently attempted fails; such an action lies without a specialty.

Because personal jurisdiction protects a waivable individual liberty interest, a court may, as a just and specifically related Rule 37 sanction, take as established the facts supporting personal jurisdiction when a defendant disobeys orders for discovery of those facts.

When a mortgagee is reasonably identifiable from a publicly recorded mortgage, due process requires that publication of a tax sale be supplemented by notice mailed to its last known available address or by personal service.

Issues identified at the pretrial conference and incorporated into the pretrial order supersede the pleadings, and pretrial orders and amendments should be construed liberally where the adversary suffers no surprise.

A federal court may defer to parallel state litigation only in exceptional circumstances, with the balance weighted heavily in favor of exercising jurisdiction, and the Federal Arbitration Act's policy of resolving doubts about arbitrability in favor of arbitration weighs against deferral.

Under New York's forum non conveniens statute, CPLR 327, the availability of an alternative forum is an important consideration but not an absolute prerequisite to dismissal; no single factor controls.

A court ordering production of sensitive files must weigh the hardship to each side and consider protective and sequencing measures, such as private inspection and redaction, and a party may obtain review of a discovery order by disobeying it and appealing the criminal contempt judgment.

To obtain a new trial for juror nondisclosure, a party must show the juror failed to answer a material voir dire question honestly and that a correct answer would have provided a valid basis for a challenge for cause.

In a case governed by New York Times v. Sullivan, appellate judges must independently determine whether the record establishes actual malice with convincing clarity, rather than reviewing that determination only for clear error under Rule 52(a).

Claim preclusion bars relitigation of the same claim between parties or their privies after a final judgment on the merits, including a default judgment, even though a default may lack issue-preclusive effect because nothing was actually litigated.

Offensive issue preclusion requires an issue actually litigated and actually and necessarily determined, and an application that does not work unfairness to the defendant; inconsistent determinations, evidence excluded from the first trial, and stipulated findings can each defeat it.

Under 28 U.S.C. section 1738, a federal court must give a state-court judgment the same claim-preclusive effect it would have in the rendering state's courts, and section 1983 creates no exception for federal claims that could have been raised in the state action.

Section 2 of the Federal Arbitration Act is substantive federal law that applies in state as well as federal courts and preempts a state law requiring a judicial forum for claims the parties agreed to arbitrate.

As the district court read the 1983 Rule 11, in a ruling later reversed on appeal, counsel violates the rule by presenting an argument for extending the law as though it were established law, or by failing to research adverse authority adequately.

A State may exercise personal jurisdiction over nonresident individuals whose own alleged intentional conduct was expressly aimed at the forum and who knew the brunt of the injury would be felt there, with each defendant's contacts assessed individually.

A class judgment binds class members under ordinary claim and issue preclusion, but only as to what was actually adjudicated: a finding of no classwide pattern or practice of discrimination does not bar class members' unadjudicated individual discrimination claims.

A foreign corporation's purchases and purchase-related training trips in a forum, a single negotiating trip there and receipt of checks drawn on a forum bank are not the continuous and systematic contacts needed for general jurisdiction over a claim unrelated to them.

A publisher's deliberate, regular circulation of its magazine in a state supports personal jurisdiction there over a libel claim based on the magazine's contents, even for nationwide damages, and the plaintiff need not have minimum contacts with the forum.
An order disqualifying counsel in a civil case is not a collateral order subject to immediate appeal under 28 U.S.C. section 1291.

Under Rule 52(a), a finding of fact is not clearly erroneous if the trial court's account of the evidence is plausible on the entire record; a choice between two permissible views of the evidence cannot be clear error, whatever the kind of evidence.
A Rule 68 offer may be a lump sum covering damages, costs and fees, and Rule 68 "costs" include attorney's fees where the underlying statute, as § 1988 does, awards fees as part of costs.

Under § 1738 a federal court must first determine a state judgment's preclusive effect under the rendering state's law; only if state law would bar the claim does the court ask whether a federal statute creates an exception, even where the later claim is exclusively federal.

A defendant who purposefully creates a substantial, continuing contractual relationship with a forum resident is subject to specific jurisdiction there on claims arising from it, without physical entry, unless he makes a compelling showing that jurisdiction would be unreasonable.

A forum may bind absent plaintiff-class members on money claims without minimum contacts if they receive the best practicable notice, a chance to be heard, a chance to opt out, and adequate representation; but it may apply its own law only to claims with sufficient forum contacts.

A state-law claim that alleges violation of a federal statute as an element does not arise under federal law where Congress is taken to have provided no private federal cause of action for that violation.

Under Rule 15(c) as it then stood, an amendment changing the party sued related back only if the new party received notice within the limitations period itself, not within the additional time allowed for service; the rule was later amended.

Under the 1983 version of Rule 11, a filing with a reasonably supportable legal and factual basis is not sanctionable merely because counsel failed to label an argument as one for changing the law or to discuss adverse authority.

Under Rule 41(a)(2), voluntary dismissal without prejudice should ordinarily be permitted unless the defendant will suffer clear legal prejudice beyond the prospect of another suit, and the possible loss of a limitations defense, absent bad faith, is not by itself such prejudice.

Once a state court has finally rejected a claim that an earlier federal judgment is preclusive, the Full Faith and Credit Act requires the federal court to give that state ruling the preclusive effect state law gives it; the Anti-Injunction Act's relitigation exception does not override that command.

Unreviewed state administrative findings do not preclude a Title VII action, but in suits under the Reconstruction civil-rights statutes federal courts must give a state agency's factfinding the preclusive effect state courts would, if the agency acted judicially and the parties had an adequate opportunity to litigate.

Failure to raise a defense or noncompulsory counterclaim ordinarily does not bar a later action, but a later action is barred if it would nullify the earlier judgment or impair rights it established and the party had a full and fair opportunity to raise the matter earlier.

On summary judgment the judge asks whether the evidence, viewed favorably to the nonmovant, could support a reasonable jury verdict under the substantive burden of proof that will apply at trial, including the clear-and-convincing standard for actual malice.

Under the artful-pleading doctrine, a plaintiff cannot defeat removal by using state-law terminology to conceal a claim's true federal nature, although a federal question must arise from the claim itself and not merely from an anticipated defense.

After adequate time for discovery, a summary-judgment movant need not negate an element on which the opponent bears the trial burden; it may point to the absence of supporting evidence in the record, and the opponent must then designate specific facts showing a genuine issue.

To survive summary judgment, an antitrust plaintiff must present evidence tending to exclude the possibility of independent action, and when the claimed conspiracy makes no economic sense the plaintiff needs more persuasive evidence than conduct equally consistent with lawful competition.

The preclusive scope of a consent judgment is measured by the parties' intent, but a claim is reserved only if the reservation is explicit, mutual, incorporated in the offer of judgment, and the reserved claim is part of the original complaint.

When a valid federal rule, fairly construed, is broad enough to collide directly with a state law, the federal rule governs in a diversity case; discretionary Federal Rule of Appellate Procedure 38 therefore displaces a state's mandatory affirmance penalty.

A proposed intervenor's different, economic motive for resisting a suit does not by itself show inadequate representation under Rule 24(a)(2); it must connect its interest to colorable defenses the existing parties are less able to assert.
The Seventh Amendment gives a defendant a jury trial on liability in a government civil action for civil penalties under the Clean Water Act, but the trial judge determines the amount of the penalty.

A statute authorizing imprisonment of a tort judgment debtor until the judgment is paid denies equal protection even under rational-basis review, because jailing an indigent debtor punishes without advancing collection.

In a section 1983 action, an unreviewed state administrative decision does not receive claim-preclusive effect merely because state law would bar the claim, although the agency's qualifying factual findings may still be given issue-preclusive effect under University of Tennessee v. Elliott.

A multidistrict transferee court deciding a question of federal law should consider the transferor circuit's precedents but is not bound by them; Van Dusen's preservation of transferor law applies to state law in diversity cases.

A party opposing summary judgment need not present evidence in final trial-admissible form; a genuine issue exists if the record, taken cumulatively, would let a jury return a verdict for the nonmoving party.

A forum court in a multistate class action must examine the law of each state whose law is claimed to conflict; where that examination shows no outcome-changing conflict, the same result may stand under each state's law.

Even where a purposeful-contact theory is available, fair play and substantial justice can defeat personal jurisdiction, as where a foreign component maker is sued in a state court on a foreign indemnity claim; no majority resolved the stream-of-commerce test.
A statutory limit on damages is an avoidance within Rule 8(c)'s residual clause, so it is an affirmative defense that the defendant waives by failing to raise it in a timely way before judgment.

The Parental Kidnaping Prevention Act does not impliedly create a private federal cause of action to determine which of two conflicting state custody decrees is valid; whether a statute implies a remedy turns on congressional intent.

When a probate nonclaim period is triggered by court-ordered proceedings and extinguishes a creditor's claim, due process requires notice by mail or a comparably reliable means to creditors who are known or reasonably ascertainable; publication suffices only for the rest.

The Hague Service Convention applies only when the forum's internal law requires documents to be transmitted abroad to complete service; where valid service on a foreign corporation is complete domestically, the Convention does not apply.

Neither the denial of an extradited defendant's claim of immunity from civil service of process nor the denial of a forum non conveniens motion to dismiss is an immediately appealable collateral order under 28 U.S.C. section 1291.

Appellate Rule 3(c)'s requirement that a notice of appeal specify the party or parties taking the appeal is jurisdictional, so a court of appeals has no jurisdiction over a party not named or otherwise adequately designated in a timely notice.

A decision on the merits is a final decision under 28 U.S.C. section 1291 whether or not a request for attorney's fees attributable to the case remains to be decided, and federal law governs that question even in diversity cases.

An order denying a Colorado River stay or dismissal is not immediately appealable under § 1291's collateral-order doctrine or as an injunction under § 1292(a)(1); the Enelow-Ettelson doctrine is overruled.

State design-defect liability for military equipment is displaced when the United States approved reasonably precise specifications, the equipment conformed to them, and the supplier warned the United States of dangers known to the supplier but not to the Government.

When a federal statute invoked in a diversity case fairly covers the disputed issue and is constitutionally valid, it governs over contrary state policy; § 1404(a) therefore controls the effect of a forum-selection clause on a motion to transfer.

A person is not bound by a judgment in litigation to which he was not a party; knowledge of the suit and a chance to intervene impose no duty to intervene, so parties who want to bind an outsider must join him.
In deciding whether complete diversity exists on removal, a court disregards the citizenship of fraudulently joined or nominal defendants and looks only to the real parties to the controversy.

A person who has filed no claim against a bankruptcy estate has a Seventh Amendment right to a jury when the trustee sues to recover an allegedly fraudulent transfer of money, even though Congress designated the action a core proceeding.

The denial of a motion to dismiss based on a contractual forum-selection clause is not immediately appealable under the collateral-order doctrine, because the right to litigate in a particular forum can be adequately vindicated on appeal after final judgment.

Under the statute then governing, a jurisdictional grant covering claims against a particular party, such as the FTCA's grant over claims against the United States, did not authorize federal courts to hear related state-law claims against additional parties lacking an independent jurisdictional basis.
Potential joint tortfeasors are merely permissive parties, not parties whose joinder is required under Rule 19(a), and Rule 19(b) is not reached unless Rule 19(a)'s threshold is satisfied.

The Seventh Amendment inquiry examines the nature of the action or issues and the nature of the remedy, giving greater importance to the remedy; damages sought from a union for breach of the duty of fair representation are legal relief triable to a jury.

A judicially adequate administrative adjudication can have issue-preclusive effect, even across agencies, but only against a party or privy, on an identical issue, and from the earlier final decision, which remains final while an appeal is pending.

A state court otherwise competent to hear a claim may not refuse a federal cause of action, or give the defendant a state-law immunity federal law does not recognize, while hearing comparable state claims; only a valid, neutral excuse will do.
In a diversity case, a §1404(a) transfer carries the transferor court's choice-of-law rules to the transferee court whether the plaintiff or the defendant sought the transfer.

A state court may exercise personal jurisdiction over a nonresident individual who is personally served while voluntarily present in the state, even though the visit is temporary and the suit is unrelated to his activities there.

Rule 32 draws no distinction between discovery depositions and depositions taken for trial; a duly noticed deposition of a witness more than one hundred miles from the courthouse where trial is held may be used for any purpose, subject to the rules of evidence.

A private litigant in a civil case may not use peremptory challenges to exclude prospective jurors on account of race, because exercising a peremptory challenge is governmental action, and the opposing litigant may assert the excluded jurors' equal-protection rights.
A person may have more than one dwelling or usual place of abode for service of process, provided each has sufficient signs of permanence; actual notice does not cure service that is otherwise void.

Under the 1983 version of Rule 11, a represented party who signs a pleading or other court paper undertakes an objective duty of reasonable inquiry; relying on counsel and subjective good faith do not excuse the failure.
Under Rule 13(g) a coparty is any party who is not an opposing party, so an original defendant may crossclaim against a third-party defendant whom a different defendant impleaded.

Federal law determines whether a state body is a court under 28 U.S.C. section 1738; quasi-judicial powers do not make an agency a court, and an unreviewed state agency decision has no issue-preclusive effect in a later Title VII action.

The amount a plaintiff claims in apparent good faith controls unless it appears to a legal certainty that the claim is for less than the jurisdictional amount, and the court must give the plaintiff a reasonable opportunity to show otherwise before dismissing.

A prejudgment attachment procedure is tested under a modified Mathews v. Eldridge balance weighing the private interest affected, the risk of erroneous deprivation and value of added safeguards, and principally the interest of the party seeking the remedy, with any ancillary government interest.

Under the 1992 rule, surveillance films of a plaintiff are litigation-preparation materials with a qualified privilege under CPLR 3101(d)(2), but those intended for trial use must be disclosed, after the plaintiff's deposition, because substantial need and undue hardship are shown.

The domestic-relations exception to diversity jurisdiction is a matter of statutory construction and bars federal courts only from issuing divorce, alimony or child-custody decrees; it does not reach tort suits between family members.

A state venue rule that treats corporations differently according to their State of incorporation does not violate equal protection if it rationally furthers the legitimate end of balancing plaintiffs' forum choices against defendants' litigation convenience.

A court may allow tightly protected discovery from an unidentified nonparty blood donor through written deposition questions under Rule 31, as modified by a Rule 26(c) protective order, where the plaintiff's need outweighs a minimal intrusion on the donor's privacy.

A document filed as an appellate brief can serve as a notice of appeal if it is filed within the time allowed by Appellate Rule 4 and gives the notice required by Rule 3(c); its title or intended role does not disqualify it.

Under § 1391(b)(2) as amended in 1990, venue lies in any district where a substantial part of the events giving rise to the claim occurred, and receipt of a debt-collection notice is such an event even if the collector did not deliberately send it there.

A trial judge's prompt oral findings, including findings adopted verbatim from a party's proposals, remain the court's findings and receive ordinary clear-error review, but unaddressed facts material to a distinct claim can still require remand.

As applied to a contractor's claim for a sum certain for work on the attached home, ex parte prejudgment attachment of real property on a judge-reviewed probable-cause affidavit, with a prompt post-attachment hearing and no creditor's bond, satisfies due process.

Dismissal with prejudice for want of prosecution is an extreme sanction, appropriate in extreme situations involving a clear record of delay or contumacious conduct, or where less drastic sanctions are unavailable.

Negligent or inadvertent delay can constitute "excusable neglect" under Bankruptcy Rule 9006(b)(1); whether it is excusable is an equitable determination taking account of all relevant circumstances, and a party is accountable for its counsel's omissions.

A timely informal brief can serve as a notice of appeal only as to judgments it designates, read liberally in its procedural context; liberal construction cannot supply notice of an appeal from an order the paper neither names nor indirectly mentions.

Once supplemental jurisdiction exists under 28 U.S.C. § 1367(a) and (b), the categories in § 1367(c) are the exclusive grounds for declining it, with the Gibbs values informing discretion within those categories rather than supplying an independent basis.

An appellee may defend a judgment on any ground supported by the record, including one the trial court rejected, but must cross-appeal to enlarge its own rights or diminish the opponent's rights under that judgment.

A federal court has no ancillary jurisdiction to enforce a settlement agreement after dismissing the suit unless the dismissal order incorporated the settlement's terms or expressly retained jurisdiction over it; otherwise enforcement needs an independent basis of federal jurisdiction.
Intentional gender discrimination in the use of peremptory challenges violates equal protection, because gender cannot serve as a proxy for an individual juror's competence or impartiality.

Mootness caused by settlement does not ordinarily justify vacating a federal civil judgment under review; vacatur is an equitable remedy that a losing party who settles can obtain only in exceptional circumstances, and a settlement term calling for vacatur is not one.

An order refusing to enforce a private settlement agreement said to confer a right not to stand trial is not an immediately appealable collateral order under § 1291, because the right can be adequately vindicated after final judgment.

Personal service on an individual physically present in the district supports personal jurisdiction, and a United Nations invitee has no immunity from service outside the headquarters district; genocide and war crimes are actionable under the Alien Tort Act without state action.

Under the 1993 version of Rule 11, sanctions sought by a party require a separate motion served twenty-one days before presentation to the court, giving a safe harbor to correct or withdraw, and a lawyer may rely on objectively reasonable client information.

Construction of a patent, including technical terms within its claims, is the exclusive responsibility of the court; the Seventh Amendment jury right attached to an infringement action does not make every subsidiary issue a jury question.

A website accessible in the forum state, without an effort by its operator to advertise, promote, sell, or otherwise target the forum, satisfies neither New York's long-arm statute nor due process as a basis for personal jurisdiction over an out-of-state defendant.

Due process does not require an innocent-owner defense to the forfeiture of property that a person entitled to use it put to unlawful use, and a lawful forfeiture is not a taking requiring compensation.
