A district court's error in failing to remand a case improperly removed for lack of complete diversity does not require vacating a final judgment on the merits if complete diversity existed when judgment was entered.

A punitive-damages award may be set aside when the demand was never mentioned in the pleadings and the opponent lacked adequate notice of it; Rule 15(b) does not cure the omission where the opponent expressly objected to submitting the issue.

Before certifying a Rule 23(b)(3) class, a court must rigorously analyze how variations in state law and the way the claims would actually be tried affect predominance and superiority; the existence of a common issue does not establish predominance.

On an interlocutory appeal under 28 U.S.C. section 1292(b), the court of appeals may decide any issue fairly included within the certified order, because the statute authorizes appeal from the order rather than only from the question the district judge identified.

In this early Internet decision, continuous online advertising and a toll-free number accessible in the forum counted as repeated solicitation under the long-arm statute and as purposeful contacts supporting personal jurisdiction.

A federal court may not abstain from deciding an uncertain state-law question merely because it is difficult, and a mandatory class restructuring a trust need not offer opt-out rights where the court has jurisdiction over the trust and representation is adequate.

Under 28 U.S.C. section 1738, a state-court judgment approving a class settlement gets the preclusive effect the rendering state would give it, even where it releases claims within exclusive federal jurisdiction, unless a federal statute creates an exception.

Where personal jurisdiction is lacking, a district court has discretion to refuse a transfer in the interest of justice even though the statute of limitations has run elsewhere, if the plaintiff was on notice of the defect and failed to protect the claim.

In diversity, a state standard limiting the size of damages awards is substantive under Erie and must be applied, but by the federal district judge in the first instance, with the court of appeals reviewing only for abuse of discretion.
Federal Rule 27(a) permits a deposition before suit only to perpetuate testimony that might otherwise be lost; it is not a device for pre-complaint discovery of the facts or of whom to sue.

The party resisting discovery bears the burden of justifying its refusal, and labelling an interrogatory a contention interrogatory does not make it premature; a party must answer with the facts it presently has and may amend or supplement later.
Whether neglect is excusable under Rule 60(b)(1) is an equitable question decided under Pioneer's factors, so ignorance of court rules by a pro se litigant is not a categorical bar to relief.

A judgment dismissing a federal claim as time-barred is a merits judgment that precludes a later state-law claim arising from the same transaction, and uncertainty whether the first court would have exercised supplemental jurisdiction does not show the lack of a full and fair opportunity to litigate.

In an action filed originally in federal court, the amount demanded in a defendant's compulsory counterclaim may be counted toward the diversity amount in controversy when the defendant answers and counterclaims without first moving to dismiss.

A class certified only for settlement must still satisfy Rule 23(a) and (b), apart from trial manageability; the fairness of the settlement under Rule 23(e) cannot substitute for predominance of common questions and adequate representation of conflicting groups within the class.

Whether Internet activity supports personal jurisdiction depends on the nature and quality of the commercial activity conducted online, on a spectrum from contracts involving knowing, repeated transmission of files into the forum, through interactive websites, to passive websites that simply make information available.

Rule 8(b) allows only an admission, a denial, or a good-faith disclaimer of knowledge or information; an answer that neither admits nor denies and demands strict proof is none of these, and the allegations so answered are deemed admitted.

Under the 1993 version of Rule 26, work-product material supplied to a retained testifying expert and considered by the expert in forming an opinion must be disclosed, whether or not the expert ultimately relied on it.

Claim preclusion by a prior federal judgment is a defense, not part of the plaintiff's properly pleaded claim, and therefore cannot support federal-question removal, even if it would dispose of the entire action.

Full faith and credit requires recognition of a sister-state judgment with no roving public-policy exception, but a state decree cannot dictate which witnesses another court may hear in a separate case brought by strangers to the decree.

A default judgment entered without valid service is void for lack of personal jurisdiction and must be vacated; actual receipt of the papers cannot by itself cure delivery to someone who is not the defendant's officer or authorized agent.

A district court conducting coordinated pretrial proceedings under 28 U.S.C. § 1407(a) may not use § 1404(a) to assign a transferred case to itself for trial, because § 1407(a) obligates the Panel to remand each action to its original district.

A section 1983 action seeking damages sounds in tort and falls within the Seventh Amendment, so predominantly factual questions of regulatory-takings liability in such an action may be submitted to a jury.

A federal district court lacks equitable authority to issue a preliminary injunction freezing an unsecured debtor's assets before judgment in a suit for contract damages where the plaintiff claims no lien or equitable interest in those assets.

An order imposing discovery-expense sanctions on an attorney under Rule 37(a)(4) is not a final decision immediately appealable under 28 U.S.C. section 1291, even when the attorney no longer represents a party in the case.

There is a presumption against giving issue-preclusive effect to findings made at criminal sentencing, overcome only when the civil plaintiff proves that preclusion is clearly fair and efficient, and such findings must be strictly necessary to the final sentence.

An interlocutory evidentiary or choice-of-law ruling in a case that then settles is not given issue-preclusive effect where it was neither essential to the judgment nor independently appealable or reviewable.

A mandatory limited-fund class under Rule 23(b)(1)(B) presumptively requires a fund independently shown to be insufficient for all claims, devotion of the whole fund to those claims, and inclusion and equitable treatment of the claimants, with conflicts addressed by separately represented subclasses.

A prima facie case combined with sufficient evidence that the employer's stated justification is false may permit, but does not compel, an inference of intentional discrimination; under Rule 50 the court reviews the whole record without weighing evidence or resolving credibility.

For a corporate Rule 30(b)(6) deposition, a designee who attends but is unprepared and unable or unwilling to supply the noticed information can be treated as not appearing, permitting Rule 37(d) monetary sanctions without a prior order compelling discovery.

In a forum non conveniens analysis a plaintiff's United States residence earns deference to the choice of a United States forum even outside the plaintiff's home district, and dismissal requires that private and public interests strongly favor the foreign forum.

Certification of state-law questions is discretionary on both sides: a state high court may decline certified questions, and, in Judge Calabresi's concurring view, the federal court should then make its best prediction of state law rather than automatically decide the federal constitutional issue.

Under Rule 41(d) a court may stay a refiled action until the plaintiff pays the costs of the earlier dismissed action and may dismiss the whole action for noncompliance; attorney fees count as such costs only where the underlying statute defines costs to include fees.

A court approving a class settlement must still find Rule 23's certification requirements met, and may approve a provision sending cash left after class claims to charity rather than back to the defendant.

When a court of appeals finds expert testimony inadmissible and the remaining evidence insufficient, it may direct entry of judgment as a matter of law for the verdict loser rather than remand for the trial court to consider a new trial.

Rule 16(f) and a court's local rules authorize sanctions, including fines payable to the court and imposed on the party itself, for failing to prepare for and participate in good faith in court-ordered mediation, even where the party relied on its counsel.

Federal common law governs the claim-preclusive effect of a federal diversity judgment and ordinarily incorporates the preclusion law of the state where the federal court sat, unless that law is incompatible with a federal interest; Rule 41(b) does not itself prescribe that effect.

A party instructing a deposition witness not to answer must expressly identify the privilege claimed with enough information to evaluate it; privileges that were, without justification, not asserted at the deposition cannot be relied on later in opposing a motion to compel.

Where only some named plaintiffs in a Title VII action satisfy the statute's special venue requirements in the chosen district, a court may cure the defect by dismissing the improperly venued plaintiffs rather than dismissing or transferring the whole action.

Under New York law applied through Rule 64, attachment as security for a future judgment requires concrete evidence of a genuine threat to enforcement, such as fraudulent disposition of assets, not merely defendants' nonresidence or a speculative possibility that assets might leave the state.

The adequacy of notice is judged under Mullane's standard of notice reasonably calculated under the circumstances, which requires a reasonable effort to inform the interested person rather than proof of actual receipt.

Court-directed service on a foreign defendant under Rule 4(f)(3) is neither a last resort nor extraordinary relief and requires no prior attempt at other methods, so long as it is not prohibited by international agreement and satisfies due process; email can qualify.

A complaint may be conditionally dismissed for failing to be short and plain when its length and excess material, here 43 pages reproducing telephone dialogue, keep it from communicating the claim clearly.

A party that fails to identify an issue for trial at the pretrial conference or in the pretrial order can waive its right to litigate that issue, even where the opposing party would bear the burden of proving it.

An employment discrimination complaint need not plead facts establishing a McDonnell Douglas prima facie case, which is a framework for proof and not a pleading requirement; it need only satisfy Rule 8(a)(2) by giving fair notice of the claim and its grounds.

A trial court may resubmit inconsistent special-verdict answers to a still-available jury, and must attempt to reconcile the jury's findings, including a revised verdict after resubmission, before ordering a new trial.

An alternative forum is inadequate for forum non conveniens purposes when a successful plaintiff would have no enforceable right to receive any award; a less generous remedy is adequate, but one so unsatisfactory that it amounts to none is not.

A plaintiff challenging a discriminatory barrier is injured by the inability to compete on equal terms and may represent a class attacking a shared policy applied through different entry routes; an automatic racial points bonus without individualized assessment is not narrowly tailored.

Electronic data is discoverable and the responding party presumptively pays for production; cost shifting may be considered only for relatively inaccessible data, such as backup tapes, under a seven-factor test in which marginal utility weighs most.

Under Rule 23(e) a class settlement must be fair, adequate and reasonable even without overt collusion; courts must scrutinize attorney's fees and unexplained larger payments to selected class members, though reasonable, individually justified incentive awards to named representatives are permitted.

Under Appellate Rule 4(a)(5), as this 2003 panel applied it, a lawyer's reliance on a nonlawyer clerk's misreading of the unambiguous appeal deadline is not excusable neglect, because the lawyer cannot delegate responsibility for knowing the rule.

Diversity is determined by the facts when the suit is filed; a change in a continuing party's citizenship after filing cannot cure a lack of diversity, unlike the dismissal of a dispensable nondiverse party.

Initial disclosure under Rule 26 covers only witnesses and documents the disclosing party may use to support its claims or defenses; other material must be sought through properly framed discovery requests, and a Rule 30(b)(6) notice cannot compel testimony from a particular employee.

A mandamus petitioner must have no other adequate means of relief, show a clear and indisputable entitlement, and persuade the court the writ is appropriate; when discovery targets the Vice President, a court may weigh separation-of-powers objections without first requiring a particularized privilege claim.

Website interactivity is not a substitute for ordinary minimum-contacts analysis; jurisdiction turns on actual forum-directed conduct and its connection to the claim, not a site's potential to transact everywhere.

A forum state must give another state's judgment the preclusive effect the rendering state would give it, so a judgment from a state that retains mutuality cannot be used for offensive nonmutual issue preclusion in the forum.

Rule 60(b)(2) relief requires evidence of facts existing at the time of decision, excusable ignorance despite due diligence, admissible evidence probably effective to change the result, and evidence not merely cumulative; such grounds cannot be reassigned to Rule 60(b)(6).

A waived jury right is not revived by an amended pleading that restates old issues, but an amendment introducing genuinely new factual issues supports a timely jury demand on those issues under Rule 38(b); Rule 39(b) relief for the old issues is discretionary.

Where complete diversity exists and at least one named plaintiff's claim satisfies the amount in controversy, § 1367 authorizes supplemental jurisdiction over related claims of additional Rule 20 plaintiffs or Rule 23 class members whose claims fall below that amount.

A state-law claim supports federal-question jurisdiction when it necessarily raises a federal issue that is actually disputed and substantial, and a federal forum can decide it without disturbing the congressionally approved balance of federal and state judicial responsibilities.

A collateral order must conclusively determine the disputed question, resolve an important issue completely separate from the merits, and be effectively unreviewable after final judgment; a claimed right to avoid trial qualifies only when delay would imperil a sufficiently substantial interest.
When a mailed notice of a tax sale is returned unclaimed before the sale, due process requires the state to take additional reasonable steps to notify the owner if it is practicable to do so.

The probate exception reserves to state probate courts only the probate or annulment of a will, the administration of an estate, and the disposition of property in a probate court's custody; it does not bar federal jurisdiction over personal claims merely related to an estate.

A federal-program insurance carrier's contract-based claim for reimbursement from an enrollee's state tort recovery does not arise under federal law; federal involvement, a federal financial interest or a federal contract does not by itself create federal-question jurisdiction.

An adequate alternative forum does not by itself require forum non conveniens dismissal; the defendant must also show that the balance of private and public interests strongly favors the foreign forum, and a resident plaintiff's choice receives deference.

A party that does not renew its evidentiary-sufficiency challenge after the verdict under Rule 50(b) cannot obtain appellate sufficiency review or a new trial on that basis; a denied preverdict Rule 50(a) motion alone does not preserve the challenge.

As the Tenth Circuit held in 2006, before the Supreme Court vacated the ruling, a prisoner alleging deliberate indifference from interrupted treatment had to plead substantial harm from the interruption itself, and conclusory allegations of harm were insufficient.

In this case-management order the court declined to pick a deposition site itself and directed counsel to settle that logistical question by one game of rock, paper, scissors, subject to place, time and review limits.

Unless Congress clearly classifies a threshold restriction on a statute's coverage as jurisdictional, courts treat it as a nonjurisdictional element of the claim; Title VII's fifteen-employee requirement is therefore an element, not a limit on subject-matter jurisdiction.

Removal of a diversity action in violation of the forum-defendant rule is a waivable, nonjurisdictional defect: the plaintiff must seek remand on that ground within thirty days, and the district court may not remand for it on its own.

Diversity jurisdiction depends on the facts existing when suit is filed: a later amendment adding a federal claim or a retroactive membership agreement cannot supply jurisdiction absent at commencement, and presence in a state does not establish domicile without the necessary intent.

When convenience, fairness, and judicial economy warrant, a federal court may dismiss on forum non conveniens grounds without first establishing its own subject-matter or personal jurisdiction, because such a dismissal is a nonmerits determination that another forum should decide the case.

Rule 8(a)(2) requires only a short and plain statement giving fair notice of the claim and its grounds, with factual allegations accepted as true on a motion to dismiss, and a pro se complaint is held to less stringent standards than lawyers' pleadings.

A district court abuses its discretion under Rule 41(a)(2) if it allows a voluntary dismissal that would cause the defendant plain legal prejudice, which includes losing a limitations defense that state law treats as a vested right extinguishing the cause of action.

A statute requiring an unauthorized insurer to post prepleading security in a court-fixed amount is construed to require an evidentiary hearing on that amount, because fixing it on the complaint alone would raise due process concerns.

The statutory time limit for filing a notice of appeal in a civil case, including the period for a reopened appeal under 28 U.S.C. section 2107(c), is jurisdictional, and courts cannot create equitable exceptions to it.

A statute authorizing emergency ex parte restraints does not displace Rule 65(b)'s procedural protections, and a no-notice asset freeze must still be justified by evidence fitting the alleged violation.

At summary judgment the evidence and reasonable inferences favor the nonmovant only where the dispute is genuine; a court need not adopt a version of the facts so plainly contradicted by the record that no reasonable jury could believe it.

Under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act, the inference of scienter must be cogent and at least as compelling as any plausible opposing inference drawn from the alleged facts, considered collectively.

A complaint must contain sufficient factual matter, accepted as true, to make entitlement to relief plausible; for a Sherman Act § 1 conspiracy claim, parallel conduct plus an unsupported assertion of agreement does not suffice.

A person is ordinarily not bound by a judgment in litigation to which that person was not a party; nonparty preclusion must rest on an established ground, not on an open-ended virtual-representation balancing of relationships and aligned interests.

Under Boyle, a government contractor is protected from state tort liability when the government approved reasonably precise specifications, the product conformed to them, and the contractor warned of dangers known to it but not to the government; knowledgeable government reordering can show approval.

The six-year limitation period of 28 U.S.C. § 2501 for claims in the Court of Federal Claims is a more absolute, jurisdictional deadline that courts must consider on their own even when the Government has waived the issue.

Excessive length alone does not justify dismissing a complaint under Rule 8 where the pleading is organized, intelligible, and clearly identifies the claims and the defendants; less drastic alternatives such as striking surplusage should be preferred to dismissal with prejudice.
An assignee holding legal title to a money claim has Article III standing to sue on it in federal court even though it has promised to remit all recovered proceeds to the assignor.

Under Rule 47(a) a trial court has broad discretion over voir dire, and questionnaires plus individual bench questioning of jurors who knew of the case give an adequate opportunity to discover bias without individualized questioning of every juror.

A preliminary-injunction applicant must show likely success on the merits, likely (not merely possible) irreparable harm without preliminary relief, a favorable balance of equities, and that an injunction is consistent with the public interest.

A denial of immunity is immediately appealable under the collateral-order doctrine only if the immunity is from suit, not merely a defense against liability; labeling a defense an immunity does not establish immediate appellate jurisdiction.

Under Rule 19(b), when a required party is a sovereign entitled to immunity and its claims to the disputed property are not frivolous, the action must be dismissed if there is a potential for injury to the absent sovereign's interests.
Whether to allow jurors to submit questions for witnesses is a matter of the trial judge's sound discretion, with the judge filtering irrelevant or argumentative questions.

Disclosure orders adverse to the attorney-client privilege are not immediately appealable as collateral orders under 28 U.S.C. section 1291, because postjudgment review and other established mechanisms sufficiently protect the privilege.

Parties to a class settlement may agree in advance that money remaining after class members have been compensated, here by treble damages, will go to related charities, and a court does not abuse its discretion in approving that disposition.

On a petition by the Chief Administrative Judge, a New York court ordered debt-collection respondents to show cause under CPLR § 5015(c) and (d) why default judgments tied to one process server's affidavits should not be vacated unless service was independently proved.

A class representative must show enough interest, credibility and understanding of the suit that he is not merely lending his name to litigation controlled by lawyers; the plaintiff bears the burden of proving adequacy with evidence at certification.

Under Rule 8, in all civil actions, a court disregards legal conclusions and unsupported recitations of elements and asks whether the remaining factual allegations, taken as true, plausibly support entitlement to relief.

When a plaintiff relies entirely on a unified fraudulent course of conduct, the claim as a whole sounds in fraud and must satisfy Rule 9(b)'s particularity requirement, even if fraud is not an element of the claim.
Rule 12(f) does not authorize a court to strike a claim for damages on the ground that the damages are precluded as a matter of law; that challenge belongs under Rule 12(b)(6) or Rule 56.

Relation back under Rule 15(c)(1)(C) depends on what the party to be added knew or should have known within the Rule 4(m) period, not on the amending plaintiff's knowledge or her timeliness in seeking to amend.

When a Federal Rule of Civil Procedure answers the same question as a state law, the Federal Rule governs in federal court if it is valid under its statutory and constitutional authorization; ordinary Erie outcome analysis does not simply override it.

To satisfy plausibility under Rule 8, a plaintiff must supply enough case-specific detail to tell a coherent story and identify the nature and grounds of the claim; plausibility is not a more-likely-than-not test.

Operating an interactive website accessible in a state does not establish specific personal jurisdiction there; the defendant must have purposefully exploited the forum market through its own deliberate conduct, and a default judgment entered without personal jurisdiction is void.

Due process does not automatically require appointed counsel for an indigent parent facing civil contempt incarceration for unpaid child support when the opposing custodian is unrepresented, provided the court uses alternative safeguards that ensure an accurate determination of ability to pay.

Federal common law is displaced when a federal statute speaks directly to the question; Congress's delegation of regulatory authority to an agency displaces it even before the agency exercises that authority.

A prisoner may seek postconviction DNA testing under § 1983 because success would not necessarily imply the invalidity of his conviction, and under Rule 8(a)(2) a complaint needs a plausible short and plain statement, not a precise exposition of legal argument.

A securities-fraud complaint may adequately plead materiality and scienter about reports of a drug's adverse effects without alleging statistically significant proof of causation; materiality is a contextual total-mix inquiry, and scienter is assessed holistically under the PSLRA and Tellabs.
A cy pres distribution of class settlement funds must be guided by the objectives of the underlying statutes and the interests of the absent class members, including the class's geographic reach.

A website operator that commercially exploits a national audience, including a substantial forum audience, and intentionally posts infringing material harming the plaintiff in the forum has expressly aimed at it and is subject to specific, though not general, jurisdiction there.

Effective service is the procedural foundation for obtaining a default judgment, and a remedy for suspect defaults may involve vacatur and a fresh opportunity to answer rather than a determination that the underlying debts do not exist.

The Federal Arbitration Act preempts a state rule, even one framed as generally applicable unconscionability, that conditions enforcement of an arbitration agreement on the availability of class procedures and so interferes with arbitration as the parties agreed to it.

A state may exercise general, all-purpose jurisdiction over a corporation only when its affiliations with the state are so continuous and systematic that it is essentially at home there; products reaching the forum through the stream of commerce do not suffice.

On the judgment in Nicastro, a foreign manufacturer that targets the United States market through an independent distributor is not subject to specific jurisdiction in a state on one isolated sale there without a regular sales flow or forum-specific effort; no rationale commanded five votes.

Rule 23(a)(2) commonality requires a common contention whose resolution can resolve an issue central to every class member's claim on a classwide basis, established through rigorous analysis; individualized monetary claims such as backpay cannot be certified under Rule 23(b)(2).

When a federal appeal turns on an unresolved question of state statutory interpretation, the court of appeals may certify the question to the state's highest court, which is better positioned to interpret the statute, and resume the appeal after that court answers.

A federal statute's permission to bring a private claim in state court does not displace the general federal-question jurisdiction of §1331 over a claim federal law creates, unless the statute excludes it expressly or by fair implication.

A court may impose an attorney-fee sanction under its inherent power only on an explicit finding of bad faith supported by clear evidence, and only after giving counsel prior notice and an opportunity to be heard.

A receivership is an extraordinary remedy to preserve property that is the subject of the litigation; a court may not place a litigant's unrelated property in receivership to pay unsecured creditors or to control vexatious litigation conduct.

A nonresident who knowingly accesses a server located in the forum state to carry out the alleged wrong uses a computer in that state under its long-arm statute, and jurisdiction over her satisfies due process.

Under 28 U.S.C. section 1407, differing legal theories do not defeat centralization of actions that share substantial factual questions; the degree of coordination or consolidation is left to the transferee judge.

Rule 23(c)(2)(B) requires individual notice to all class members identifiable through reasonable effort; the expense or size of a search does not excuse it where available records can identify actual members, and an accurate partial list requires notice even when a complete one is impracticable.

A turnover order under New York CPLR § 5225(b) requires that the garnishee itself have actual possession or custody of the debtor's assets; practical control of a subsidiary that holds them is constructive possession and does not suffice.

Under New York CPLR § 5225(b), a turnover order may issue only against an entity that itself has actual possession or custody of the judgment debtor's property; constructive possession through practical control of a subsidiary is insufficient.

Under Rule 8(d) a complaint may plead inconsistent factual allegations, so a plausible discrimination claim is not defeated at the pleading stage merely because the complaint also identifies another, lawful reason for the decision; but-for cause is not sole cause.

Securities-fraud plaintiffs invoking the fraud-on-the-market presumption need not prove materiality to obtain Rule 23(b)(3) certification, because materiality is an objective question common to the class whose failure defeats every member's claim; merits questions are considered at certification only as relevant to Rule 23.

A contractual waiver of class arbitration is enforceable under the FAA even when the cost of individually proving a federal statutory claim exceeds the potential recovery; the expense of proving a claim does not eliminate the right to pursue the remedy.

An order compelling disclosure of assertedly attorney-client privileged material in civil litigation is not immediately appealable, even when directed to the litigant's counsel, because review after final judgment ordinarily protects the privilege adequately.

A defendant's uniform payment methodology does not by itself establish commonality or predominance; the plaintiff must prove that its legality can be decided classwide, which requires accounting for differences in class members' contractual rights and circumstances.

A forum-selection clause does not make statutorily proper venue improper; a valid clause naming another federal district is enforced through § 1404(a), with the plaintiff's forum choice and private interests given no weight and only public-interest factors left to resist transfer.

Federal jurisdiction over a state-created claim requires a federal issue that is necessarily raised, actually disputed, substantial to the federal system as a whole, and capable of resolution in federal court without disrupting the congressionally approved division of responsibility between federal and state courts.

A stipulation by a proposed class representative cannot reduce the amount in controversy for Class Action Fairness Act jurisdiction unless it legally binds the absent proposed class members, which a precertification stipulation does not.

Specific personal jurisdiction requires the defendant's own suit-related conduct to connect it to the forum; the plaintiff's location, foreseeable injury there, sales not linked to the alleged wrong, an email list with forum subscribers, or an interactive website do not suffice.

A complaint that adequately states the facts showing entitlement to relief may not be rejected merely because it fails to cite the legal theory or statute, such as 42 U.S.C. section 1983, on which the claim rests.

Before granting preliminary approval of a class settlement, a court must have a record that lets it judge whether the proposal falls within the range of possible approval; the parties' assurances that a capped fund is adequate do not suffice.

A court will not order alternative service under Rule 4(f)(3), even where conventional service appears impracticable, unless competent evidence shows the proposed method is reasonably calculated to reach the particular defendant.

A court may exercise general jurisdiction over a corporation only where its affiliations make it essentially at home, paradigmatically its place of incorporation and principal place of business; a substantial, continuous, and systematic course of business in the State is not enough.

A notice of removal under section 1446(a) needs only a plausible allegation that the amount in controversy exceeds the jurisdictional threshold; evidence establishing the amount is required only when the plaintiff contests, or the court questions, the allegation.

Under either prong of the qualified-immunity inquiry, a court ruling on summary judgment must credit the nonmoving party's competent evidence and draw reasonable inferences in that party's favor, and may not define the factual context by resolving genuinely disputed facts for the movant.

Specific personal jurisdiction requires that the defendant's own suit-related conduct create a substantial connection with the forum state itself; the plaintiff's forum connections, or an injury the plaintiff feels there, cannot be the only link, even for intentional torts.

A defendant's cross-complaint reduces or defeats a prejudgment attachment only if the defendant shows the probable validity of its own claim; merely filing a larger offsetting claim does not bar attachment.

An appellee may defend a judgment on any ground in the record without a cross-appeal, so long as he does not seek to enlarge his own rights or lessen his opponent's under the judgment; such a defense in a habeas appeal needs no certificate of appealability.

The Federal Arbitration Act preempts a state court's interpretation of a contract that does not place arbitration agreements on equal footing with other contracts, such as reading a reference to state law to include state law already invalidated by federal law.

Rule 23 governs in federal court despite a state statute barring private class actions on a state-created claim, because allowing the class changes only the mode of litigating existing rights, not the substantive rights themselves.

Class notice must be the best practicable under the circumstances, not a guarantee of actual receipt, and a settlement reached before certification is also examined for signs of collusion before approval.

A settlement class must independently satisfy Rule 23(a) and (b)(3); separately represented subclasses and an uncapped, inflation-protected fund can resolve the conflict between presently injured and future claimants, and the settlement must be fair, reasonable, and adequate under Rule 23(e).

A witness is otherwise made known during discovery under Rule 26(e) only if the information is the functional equivalent of a proper disclosure; a passing deposition mention does not qualify, and Rule 37(c)(1) bars the undisclosed witness unless the omission was substantially justified or harmless.

Under Iqbal a complaint must plead facts permitting a reasonable inference that each official violated the Constitution through his own conduct; supervisory rank alone is insufficient, but detailed allegations of knowledge, approval and deliberate indifference can satisfy that standard.

Under Erie there is no free-standing national common law of insurance; a federal diversity court must identify an applicable state's law, ordinarily by applying the forum state's conflicts principles under Klaxon.

Counsel must confer and cooperate in developing electronic search methodology, including search terms, under Rule 26(f)(3)(C) and local rules; and a motion to compel production filed before the response deadline has expired is premature.

A state must give full faith and credit to a sister-state judgment that appears on its face to come from a court of general jurisdiction unless jurisdiction is disproved; a mandatory rule of decision is not a limit on subject-matter jurisdiction.

A court may approve a class settlement that requires arbitration of future disputes when, on the Grinnell factors and in context, the settlement is fair, as where the class consists of sophisticated businesses, none objected, and the defendants insisted on the term.

Evidence Rule 412 governs admissibility at trial and does not bar discovery; whether a nonparty must produce documents is decided under Rule 26 relevance and proportionality and Rule 45, with privacy interests protected by tailored limits and a protective order.

A mass-tort settlement class may be certified under Rule 23(b)(3) where the defendant's alleged common course of conduct supplies commonality and predominance and separately represented subclasses with an uncapped fund protect future claimants; approval is reviewed for abuse of discretion.

A court may order email service abroad under Rule 4(f)(3) when no international agreement prohibits it and the movant supplies facts showing that process sent to the address is likely to reach the defendant.

Under Rule 8(b) an answer must admit or deny each portion of every allegation or state a genuine lack of knowledge after reasonable inquiry, and it may not decline to respond because an allegation states a legal conclusion.

Under Rule 26(b)(1) discovery must be relevant and proportional to the needs of the case, and in a products-liability case discovery of other designs is measured on a sliding scale of similarity to the product at issue.

A failure-to-state-a-claim defense omitted from an earlier Rule 12 motion is preserved but must be raised in a pleading, a Rule 12(c) motion, or at trial; a district court's consideration of it in a successive pre-answer motion may be harmless error.

When a conviction is invalidated and no retrial will occur, due process requires the state to refund fees, costs and restitution exacted because of the conviction, and the state may not make the defendant prove innocence to get the money back.

A federal charter's sue-and-be-sued clause that refers to any court of competent jurisdiction, state or federal, gives the entity capacity to litigate but does not itself confer federal subject-matter jurisdiction; an independent jurisdictional source is required.

Plaintiffs denied class treatment cannot create a final decision appealable under 28 U.S.C. § 1291 by voluntarily dismissing their individual claims with prejudice; that device would undermine the final-judgment rule and Rule 23(f)'s discretionary review of class orders.

A fee award imposed under a federal court's inherent authority through civil procedures must be compensatory, not punitive: it is limited to the fees the innocent party would not have incurred but for the misconduct.

Where a juror's overt statement shows that racial animus was a significant motivating factor in the vote to convict, the Sixth Amendment requires the no-impeachment rule to yield so the trial court can consider the evidence.

State officers may arrest and hold a person only with authority under state law; Massachusetts common law and statutes give court officers no power to hold an otherwise releasable person solely on a federal civil immigration detainer.

A later suit is barred as improper claim-splitting if the first pending action, assuming it were final, would preclude the second because both involve the same parties or their privies and arise from the same transaction or series of transactions.

The Federal Arbitration Act preempts a state rule that singles out arbitration agreements for disfavored treatment, including a rule about contract formation that requires a power of attorney to state expressly that the agent may waive the principal's rights to court access and jury trial.

Atlantic Marine's forum-selection presumption applies to the parties who agreed to the clause, not the whole lawsuit; courts analyze contracting and noncontracting parties separately and then consider jurisdiction, joinder, severance and transfer.

A mutual settlement for consideration of remaining individual claims after continued litigation, expressly reserving specified issues for appeal, produces a final judgment under 28 U.S.C. section 1291; Microsoft v. Baker's bar on manufactured finality does not apply.

Purposeful availment ordinarily requires affirmative conduct directed toward the forum, not merely a failure to prevent access from it, so a website operator's ability to geoblock forum users does not by itself make its failure to do so forum targeting.

An order labeled a temporary restraining order is reviewable on appeal if it has the qualities of a preliminary injunction, which ordinarily requires that it was strongly challenged in adversarial proceedings and will remain in effect beyond Rule 65(b)'s fourteen-day period.

A Bivens claim that differs meaningfully from Bivens, Davis v. Passman and Carlson v. Green presents a new context, and courts must not imply a damages remedy there if special factors counsel hesitation absent congressional authorization.

A state court may exercise general jurisdiction over a corporation only where it is essentially at home, ordinarily its place of incorporation and principal place of business, and FELA's section 56 governs venue and subject-matter jurisdiction, not personal jurisdiction.
Rule 23 does not require class representatives to demonstrate an administratively feasible way to identify absent class members as a separate prerequisite to class certification.

Specific personal jurisdiction requires an affiliation between the forum and the particular claims at issue, and a defendant's extensive but unrelated forum contacts cannot substitute for that connection.

A court may allow discovery before the Rule 26(f) conference on good cause, meaning the discovery is needed for the suit to progress, if the plaintiff has a good-faith basis for personal jurisdiction, and may attach conditions protecting the person to be identified.

Discovery about similar incidents is relevant when it bears on a defendant's knowledge and the reasonableness of its procedures, but requests still need time and subject limits, and a party objecting on proportionality grounds must make a specific showing, not merely recite the Rule 26 factors.

Reasonable corrective-discovery costs caused by an opponent's discovery misconduct may be shifted as a compensatory sanction even when they exceed the likely damages on the underlying claim; that disproportion does not make the sanction punitive.
Preserving an objection to the legal standard for a fee sanction does not preserve entry-specific objections under that standard that the party never presented to the district court.

Under Rule 4(f)(3) a court may authorize email service on foreign defendants without first requiring other methods, if no international agreement prohibits it and the email addresses are shown to be reasonably calculated to give notice.

Rule 4(f)(3) court-directed service is an available method rather than a last resort, and a court may authorize service on foreign defendants through their United States counsel when that is not prohibited by international agreement and is reasonably calculated to give notice.

Personal jurisdiction over a foreign website operator requires the operator's own suit-related conduct directed at the forum; universal website access, the independent acts of users and advertising intermediaries, and an unused ability to geoblock are not enough.

When one of several cases consolidated under Rule 42(a) is finally decided, the losing party may immediately appeal that decision under section 1291, because consolidation does not merge the constituent cases or eliminate their separate identities.

Under § 1608(a)(3) of the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act, a service packet for a foreign state must be mailed directly to the foreign minister at the minister's office in the foreign state, not to the state's embassy in the United States.

Rule 23(f)'s fourteen-day deadline is a nonjurisdictional claim-processing rule, but it is mandatory when properly invoked and cannot be equitably tolled because Appellate Rule 26(b) expressly prohibits extending the time to petition for permission to appeal.

Whether federal law preempts a state-law failure-to-warn claim because the FDA would not have approved the warning is a question for the judge, including subsidiary factual disputes, not for the jury.

Issue preclusion ordinarily binds parties on issues actually litigated, resolved, and essential to a valid prior judgment, but an intervening change in the applicable legal context can justify an exception that removes the earlier determination's preclusive force.
When parties have validly delegated the question of arbitrability to an arbitrator, a court may not decide that question itself, even if it thinks the argument for arbitration is wholly groundless.

Neither the general removal statute, § 1441(a), nor CAFA's removal provision, § 1453(b), permits removal by a third-party counterclaim defendant, because the defendant who may remove is the defendant to the original plaintiff's complaint.

Generally applicable rules fixing qualifications are legislative acts that receive only the process inherent in lawmaking, while individual adjudicative decisions may require further safeguards under Mathews v. Eldridge; conditioning felons' re-enfranchisement on paying sentence obligations receives rational-basis review.

CERCLA's grant of exclusive federal jurisdiction over controversies arising under the Act does not strip state courts of jurisdiction over state-law claims, although CERCLA may still restrict a particular remedy, such as restoration work requiring EPA approval.

A foreign forum can be an adequate alternative for forum non conveniens purposes if it offers a meaningful remedy for the same injury, even where its law channels liability to a party other than the defendant sued.

An American plaintiff's choice of a domestic forum receives a strong presumption of convenience that is not reduced merely because the plaintiff invested abroad or sued alongside foreign coplaintiffs, and a defendant must support forum non conveniens with evidence.

Certification of an unsettled state-law question is discretionary, not obligatory, but in exceptional cases a federal court should certify novel state-law questions to the state's highest court before deciding a constitutional question that depends on them.

Federal courts may fashion federal common law only where necessary to protect uniquely federal interests; absent such an interest, state law decides how a consolidated tax refund is allocated among members of a corporate group.

There is no free-standing "defense preclusion": a defense not litigated in an earlier suit is barred only if claim or issue preclusion applies, and claim preclusion does not apply where the later suit raises a different claim.

Lawful permanent residence does not make an alien a United States citizen for diversity purposes, so section 1332(a)(2) gives no jurisdiction over a suit between two aliens, and a treaty's access-to-courts provision does not supply it.

In a nationwide Rule 23 class action under a federal statute, the named representative must establish personal jurisdiction over the defendant, but no separate showing of specific jurisdiction is required for each absent class member's claim.

When a defendant removes a case in part under §1442 or §1443, the exception in §1447(d) permits appellate review of the district court's entire remand order, including every removal ground the order rejected.

A defendant seeking forum non conveniens dismissal from the plaintiff's home forum bears a heavy burden; an equal or marginal balance does not suffice, and a court abuses its discretion by clearly misweighing the materiality of witnesses and claims.

Attorneys who file and keep pursuing litigation without an objectively reasonable inquiry into its legal and factual premises, or for an improper purpose, may be sanctioned under Rule 11, § 1927 and inherent authority, whatever their asserted personal belief.

A court may dismiss on its own initiative only by a fair procedure, generally notice and a meaningful opportunity to respond, and a party must have a full and fair opportunity to discover information essential to opposing summary judgment.

The ultimate fair-use question is a mixed question that predominantly involves legal work and is reviewed de novo, while underlying jury findings of fact receive deference, and that allocation does not violate the Seventh Amendment.

A website's accessibility, interactivity, and unrelated advertising or merchandise sales in the forum do not support specific jurisdiction over a libel claim unless the publisher purposefully directed the allegedly wrongful conduct at the forum.

Specific jurisdiction over an out-of-state online critic requires the defendant's own conduct aimed at the forum; knowledge that the plaintiff lives there and foreseeable injury there are not enough, and a court may refuse to transfer a case filed in an improper forum in apparent bad faith.

Every class member must have Article III standing to recover individual damages, which requires a concrete injury; a statutory violation alone does not suffice, and an unmaterialized risk of future harm does not by itself support standing for retrospective damages.

Specific jurisdiction requires that the claim arise out of or relate to the defendant's forum contacts, and relate to does not demand causation: a manufacturer that systematically serves a state's market for a model may be sued there when that model injures a resident there.

An All Writs Act order enabling a habeas prisoner to search for new evidence is not necessary or appropriate in aid of federal habeas jurisdiction unless the prisoner shows the evidence would be admissible in connection with a particular claim for relief.

A judge's error of law is a 'mistake' under Rule 60(b)(1), whether or not obvious, so a motion asserting one is subject to the one-year limit of Rule 60(c)(1) and cannot be brought under Rule 60(b)(6).

A statutory limit is jurisdictional only if Congress clearly says so; Bankruptcy Code § 363(m), which limits the effect of a successful appeal on certain completed sales and leases, constrains appellate remedies and is not jurisdictional.
The exhaustion requirement of § 1252(d)(1) is nonjurisdictional and subject to waiver and forfeiture, and it does not require a noncitizen to seek discretionary review such as Board reconsideration.
A procedural requirement is jurisdictional only when Congress clearly says so; the Quiet Title Act's twelve-year time bar, 28 U.S.C. § 2409a(g), is a nonjurisdictional claims-processing rule.
A post-trial motion under Rule 50 is not required to preserve for appellate review a purely legal issue resolved at summary judgment.

A court that finds apparently nonexistent authorities in a filing may order counsel to show cause why sanctions should not be imposed under Rule 11(b)(2) and (c), 28 U.S.C. § 1927, and its inherent power, giving notice and a chance to respond.

Rule 11(b)(2) requires a reasonable inquiry that legal contentions rest on existing law; court-initiated sanctions require subjective bad faith, which knowing falsehoods or conscious avoidance can establish, and absent exceptional circumstances the lawyer's firm is jointly responsible.

The Due Process Clause does not prohibit a state from exercising general jurisdiction over a foreign corporation that registered to do business under a statute expressly making registration a basis for such jurisdiction; Pennsylvania Fire controls and International Shoe did not overrule it.

A procedural requirement is jurisdictional only if Congress clearly gives it that character; the sixty-day deadline in 5 U.S.C. § 7703(b)(1) for petitioning the Federal Circuit to review a Merit Systems Protection Board decision is nonjurisdictional.
Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code does not authorize a plan provision that releases and enjoins claims against a nondebtor without the consent of the affected claimants.

To state a First Amendment claim of coercion through intermediaries, a plaintiff must plausibly allege conduct that, in context, could reasonably be understood as threatening adverse government action to punish or suppress the plaintiff's speech.

A party seeking to reopen a final judgment in order to amend its complaint must first satisfy Rule 60(b)(6)'s extraordinary-circumstances requirement on its own terms; Rule 15(a)'s liberal amendment standard applies only after reopening and cannot dilute that requirement.

An employer must prove that an employee falls within a Fair Labor Standards Act exemption by a preponderance of the evidence, the default standard in civil litigation when a statute does not specify another.

The general equitable authority granted by the Judiciary Act of 1789 likely does not permit a universal injunction; an injunction may not reach further than necessary to give complete relief to each plaintiff with standing.

Under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act, § 1330(b), personal jurisdiction over a foreign state exists when an immunity exception supplies subject-matter jurisdiction and service complies with § 1608; the statute requires no additional minimum-contacts showing.

The thirty-day deadline in § 1252(b)(1) for petitioning for review of a final removal order is a nonjurisdictional claim-processing rule; a FARO issued in the streamlined removal process is final upon issuance, despite later withholding-only proceedings.

To invoke PLCAA's predicate exception on an aiding-and-abetting theory, a complaint must plausibly allege conscious, culpable and affirmative assistance of unlawful firearm sales; knowledge that some unidentified dealers break the law and failure to stop them is not enough.
A voluntary dismissal without prejudice under Rule 41(a) is a final proceeding from which a district court may grant relief under Rule 60(b).

The Fifth Amendment's Due Process Clause does not incorporate the Fourteenth Amendment's minimum-contacts standard; a narrow statute reasonably linking jurisdiction over the PLO and PA to conduct involving the United States and sensitive foreign-policy matters satisfies Fifth Amendment due process.

Under the Prison Litigation Reform Act, parties are entitled to a jury determination of disputed exhaustion facts when those facts are intertwined with the merits of a claim that carries a Seventh Amendment jury right.

When a plaintiff properly amends a removed complaint to delete every federal question, leaving only state-law claims, the federal court loses supplemental jurisdiction along with federal-question jurisdiction and must remand the case to state court.
A motion under Rule 60(b)(4) for relief from an allegedly void judgment must, like every Rule 60(b) motion, be made within a reasonable time under Rule 60(c)(1).
The thirty-day deadline for removal in 28 U.S.C. § 1446(b)(1) is nonjurisdictional but mandatory, and a court may not equitably toll it.

An agency's preliminary nonjury findings and forfeiture order do not violate the Seventh Amendment where the order is not binding and, before payment can be compelled, the party can insist on a jury's ultimate determination in a de novo enforcement action.

A pretrial denial of Yearsley protection to a federal contractor is not immediately appealable under the collateral-order doctrine, because Yearsley is a defense to liability rather than an immunity from suit and can be effectively reviewed after final judgment.

To plead induced patent infringement under 35 U.S.C. § 271(b), a complaint must plausibly allege affirmative, purposeful encouragement of infringement, which may be implicit, not merely statements that a third party might conceivably understand as encouragement.
An erroneous interlocutory dismissal of a nondiverse defendant, reversed on appeal, does not cure a lack of complete diversity that existed at removal, so the federal merits judgment must be vacated.

When a valid Federal Rule of Civil Procedure answers the disputed question, it displaces contrary state law in federal court even if the state rule would count as substantive under ordinary Erie analysis; Rule 8 displaces Delaware's affidavit-of-merit requirement.

Where a defendant undertook to cure an animal and allegedly performed the cure so negligently that it died, a special writ suited to that negligent performance was held sufficient, rather than covenant or general trespass.
